**Gwen Renée Stefani Shelton** ([/s t ə ˈ f ɑː n i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/5/5c/En-us-Stefani.wav/En-us-Stefani.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-Stefani.wav "File:En-us-Stefani.wav")[_stə-FAH-nee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); née **Stefani**, formerly **Rossdale**; born October 3, 1969) is an American singer, songwriter and fashion designer. Stefani rose to fame as a member and lead vocalist of the band [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt"), whose hit singles include "[Just a Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_a_Girl "Just a Girl")", "[Spiderwebs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiderwebs_(song) "Spiderwebs (song)")", and "[Don't Speak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Speak "Don't Speak")" from their studio album _[Tragic Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragic\_Kingdom "Tragic Kingdom")_ (1995), as well as "[Hey Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_Baby_(No_Doubt_song) "Hey Baby (No Doubt song)")" and "[It's My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_My_Life_(Talk_Talk_song)#No_Doubt_version "It's My Life (Talk Talk song)")" from later albums. During the band's hiatus, Stefani embarked on a solo [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") career in 2004 by releasing her debut studio album _[Love. Angel. Music. Baby.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love.\_Angel.\_Music.\_Baby. "Love. Angel. Music. Baby.")_ Inspired by pop music from the 1980s, the album was a critical and commercial success.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-nme-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hb-9) It spawned six singles, including "[What You Waiting For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_You_Waiting_For%3F "What You Waiting For?")", "[Rich Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Girl_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Rich Girl (Gwen Stefani song)")", "[Hollaback Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollaback_Girl "Hollaback Girl")", and "[Cool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Cool (Gwen Stefani song)")". "Hollaback Girl" reached number one on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart while also becoming the first US download to sell one million copies.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-RSMillion-10)

Stefani's second studio album, _[The Sweet Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sweet\_Escape "The Sweet Escape")_ (2006), yielded the singles "[Wind It Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_It_Up_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Wind It Up (Gwen Stefani song)")" and the [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweet_Escape_(song) "The Sweet Escape (song)"), the latter of which was number three on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") year-end chart of 2007.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-11) Her third solo album, _[This Is What the Truth Feels Like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_What\_the\_Truth\_Feels\_Like "This Is What the Truth Feels Like")_ (2016), was her first solo album to reach number one on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart. Her fourth solo album and first full-length [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music") album, _[You Make It Feel Like Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Make\_It\_Feel\_Like\_Christmas "You Make It Feel Like Christmas")_, was released in 2017 and charted 19 tracks on _Billboard_'s [Holiday Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") component chart in the United States. Stefani has released several singles with husband [Blake Shelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Shelton "Blake Shelton"), including "[Nobody but You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody_but_You_(Blake_Shelton_and_Gwen_Stefani_song) "Nobody but You (Blake Shelton and Gwen Stefani song)")" (2020), which reached number 18 in the US. In 2024, she released her fifth studio album _[Bouquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouquet\_(Gwen\_Stefani\_album) "Bouquet (Gwen Stefani album)")_.

[Stefani's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Gwen_Stefani "List of awards and nominations received by Gwen Stefani") include three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), an [American Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award "American Music Award"), a [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award"), a [World Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Music_Award "World Music Award"), and two [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award"). She received a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") in 2023. In 2003, she debuted her clothing line [L.A.M.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.M.B. "L.A.M.B.") and expanded her collection with the 2005 Harajuku Lovers line inspired by [Japanese culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Japan "Culture of Japan") and fashion. _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ magazine ranked Stefani the 54th most successful artist and 37th most successful Hot 100 artist of the 2000–2009 decade.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-13)[VH1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1 "VH1") ranked her 13th on their "100 Greatest Women in Music" list in 2012.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-Vh1-14)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Gwen Renée Stefani was born on October 3, 1969, in [Fullerton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fullerton,_California "Fullerton, California"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-allmusic-15) and raised [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") in nearby [Anaheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) She was named after a stewardess in the 1968 novel _[Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airport\_(Hailey\_novel) "Airport (Hailey novel)")_, and her middle name, Renée, comes from the [Four Tops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Tops "Four Tops")' 1967 version of [the Left Banke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Left_Banke "The Left Banke")'s 1966 song "[Walk Away Renée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_Away_Ren%C3%A9e "Walk Away Renée")".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-17) Her father, Dennis Stefani, is [Italian American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Americans "Italian Americans") and worked as a [Yamaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_Corporation "Yamaha Corporation") marketing executive.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-parents-18) Her mother, Patti Stefani ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Flynn[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-Patti_Flynn-19)), is [Irish-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Americans "Irish Americans")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-20) and worked as an accountant before becoming a homemaker.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-parents-18)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-family-21) Stefani's parents were fans of [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") and exposed her to music by artists like [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") and [Emmylou Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmylou_Harris "Emmylou Harris").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) Stefani has two younger siblings, Jill and Todd, and an older brother, [Eric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stefani "Eric Stefani").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-family-21) Before leaving No Doubt to pursue an animation career on _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_, Eric was the band's keyboardist.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-allmusic-15)

She attended [Loara High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loara_High_School "Loara High School"), where she graduated in 1987.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-22) After high school, she attended [Fullerton College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fullerton_College "Fullerton College") and [Cypress College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cypress_College "Cypress College").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-24) She then transferred to [California State University, Fullerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Fullerton "California State University, Fullerton"), but dropped out to pursue her music career.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-25)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1986–2004: Career beginnings and No Doubt

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1986–2004: Career beginnings and No Doubt")]

Main article: [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt")

Her brother Eric introduced Gwen to [2 Tone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Tone_(music_genre) "2 Tone (music genre)") music by [Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madness_(band) "Madness (band)") and [The Selecter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Selecter "The Selecter"). Eric and Gwen had originally started a band named Applecore. Then in 1986, he invited her to provide vocals for No Doubt, a [ska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ska "Ska") band he was forming. She later became the sole lead singer when the other singer, John Spence, took his own life in December 1987.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-allmusic-15) In 1991, the band was signed to [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-26) The band released its [self-titled debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt_(No_Doubt_album) "No Doubt (No Doubt album)") in 1992, but its ska-pop sound was unsuccessful due to the popularity of [grunge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grunge "Grunge").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-27) Before the mainstream success of both No Doubt and [Sublime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sublime_(band) "Sublime (band)"), Stefani contributed guest vocals to "Saw Red" on Sublime's 1994 album _[Robbin' the Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbin'\_the\_Hood "Robbin' the Hood")_. Stefani rejected the aggressiveness of female grunge artists and cited [Blondie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blondie_(band) "Blondie (band)") singer [Debbie Harry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Harry "Debbie Harry")'s combination of power and [sex appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_appeal "Sex appeal") as a major influence.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-anniversary-28) No Doubt's third album, _[Tragic Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragic\_Kingdom "Tragic Kingdom")_ (1995), which followed the self-released _[The Beacon Street Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Beacon\_Street\_Collection "The Beacon Street Collection")_ (1995), took more than three years to make. Five singles were released from _Tragic Kingdom_, including "[Don't Speak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Speak "Don't Speak")", which led the [Hot 100 Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100_Airplay_(Radio_Songs) "Hot 100 Airplay (Radio Songs)") year-end chart of 1997.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-29) Stefani left college for one semester to tour for _Tragic Kingdom_ but did not return when touring lasted two and a half years.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) The album was nominated for a Grammy and sold more than 16 million copies worldwide by 2004.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-31) In late 2000, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ magazine named her "the Queen of Confessional Pop".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-32)

During the time when No Doubt was receiving mainstream success, Stefani collaborated on the singles "You're the Boss" with [the Brian Setzer Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brian_Setzer_Orchestra "The Brian Setzer Orchestra"), "[South Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side_(song) "South Side (song)")" with [Moby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moby "Moby"), and "[Let Me Blow Ya Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_Me_Blow_Ya_Mind "Let Me Blow Ya Mind")" with [Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eve_(rapper) "Eve (rapper)"). No Doubt released the less popular _[Return of Saturn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_Saturn "Return of Saturn")_ in 2000, which expanded upon the [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") influences of _Tragic Kingdom_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-33) Most of the lyrical content focused on Stefani's often rocky relationship with then-[Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_(British_band) "Bush (British band)") frontman [Gavin Rossdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Rossdale "Gavin Rossdale") and her insecurities, including indecision on settling down and having a child.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-34) The band's 2001 album, _[Rock Steady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_Steady\_(album) "Rock Steady (album)")_, explored more [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae") and [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") sounds, while maintaining the band's new wave influences.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-35) The album generated career-highest singles chart positions in the United States,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-36) and "[Hey Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_Baby_(No_Doubt_song) "Hey Baby (No Doubt song)")" and "[Underneath It All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underneath_It_All "Underneath It All")" received Grammy Awards. A greatest hits collection, _[The Singles 1992–2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Singles\_1992%E2%80%932003 "The Singles 1992–2003")_, which includes a [cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") of [Talk Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_Talk "Talk Talk")'s "[It's My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_My_Life_(Talk_Talk_song) "It's My Life (Talk Talk song)")", was released in 2003. In 2002, Eve and Stefani won a [Grammy Award for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap/Sung_Collaboration "Grammy Award for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration") for "Let Me Blow Ya Mind".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-37)

### 2004–2006: Solo debut and other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2004–2006: Solo debut and other ventures")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/WhatYouWaitingFor1.jpg/250px-WhatYouWaitingFor1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WhatYouWaitingFor1.jpg)

Stefani performing "[What You Waiting For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_You_Waiting_For%3F "What You Waiting For?")" during the [Harajuku Lovers Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku_Lovers_Tour "Harajuku Lovers Tour") in 2005

Stefani's debut solo album, _[Love. Angel. Music. Baby.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love.\_Angel.\_Music.\_Baby. "Love. Angel. Music. Baby.")_, was released on November 12, 2004. The album features several collaborations with producers and other artists, including [Tony Kanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Kanal "Tony Kanal"), [Tom Rothrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Rothrock "Tom Rothrock"), [Linda Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Perry "Linda Perry"), [André 3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_3000 "André 3000"), [Nellee Hooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellee_Hooper "Nellee Hooper"), [the Neptunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Neptunes "The Neptunes") and [New Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Order_(band) "New Order (band)"). Stefani created the album to modernize the music she had listened to in high school, and _L.A.M.B._ takes influence from a variety of music styles of the 1980s and early 1990s such as new wave, synthpop, and [electro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electro_(music) "Electro (music)").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-38) Stefani's decision to use her solo career as an opportunity to delve further into pop music instead of trying "to convince the world of [her] talent, depth and artistic worth" was considered unusual.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-nme-8) The album was described as "fun as hell but... not exactly rife with [subversive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subversion "Subversion") social commentary".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-39) The album debuted on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") albums chart at number seven, selling 309,000 copies in its first week.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-40)_L.A.M.B._ reached multi-platinum status in the United States,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-parents-18) the United Kingdom,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-41) Australia,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-42) and Canada.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-43)

The first single from the album "[What You Waiting For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_You_Waiting_For%3F "What You Waiting For?")", co-written by [Linda Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Perry "Linda Perry"), debuted atop the ARIA Singles Chart, charted at number 47 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hot100-44) and reached the top ten on most other charts.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-45) The song served to explain why Stefani produced a solo album and discusses her fears in leaving No Doubt for a solo career[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-46) as well as her desire to have a baby.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-guardian-47) "[Rich Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Girl_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Rich Girl (Gwen Stefani song)")" was released as the album's second single. A duet with rapper [Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eve_(rapper) "Eve (rapper)"), and produced by [Dr. Dre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), it is an adaptation of a 1990s pop song by British musicians [Louchie Lou & Michie One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louchie_Lou_&_Michie_One "Louchie Lou & Michie One"), which itself is a very loose [cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") lyrically but closer melodically of "[If I Were a Rich Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Were_a_Rich_Man_(song) "If I Were a Rich Man (song)")", from the musical _[Fiddler on the Roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler\_on\_the\_Roof "Fiddler on the Roof")_. "Rich Girl" reached the US and UK top ten.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hot100-44)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-ukchart-48) The album's third single "[Hollaback Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollaback_Girl "Hollaback Girl")" became Stefani's first US and second Australian number-one single; it reached top ten elsewhere.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hot100-44)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-49) The song was the first US [music download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") to sell more than one million copies, and its [brass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass_instrument "Brass instrument")-driven composition remained popular throughout 2005.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-RSMillion-10) The fourth single "[Cool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Cool (Gwen Stefani song)")" was released shortly following the popularity of its predecessor, reaching the top 20 in US and UK.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hot100-44)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-ukchart-48) The song's lyrics and its accompanying music video, filmed on [Lake Como](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Como "Lake Como"), depict Stefani's former relationship with Kanal.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-Vineyard_mtv-50) "[Luxurious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxurious "Luxurious")" was released as the album's fifth single, but did not perform as well as its predecessors. "[Crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Crash (Gwen Stefani song)")" was released in January 2006 as the album's sixth single in lieu of _Love. Angel. Music. Baby._'s sequel, which Stefani postponed because of her pregnancy.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-pregnant-51)

In 2004, Stefani showed interest in making film appearances and began auditioning for films such as _[Mr. & Mrs. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_&\_Mrs.\_Smith\_(2005\_film) "Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)")_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-52) She made her film debut playing [Jean Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Harlow "Jean Harlow") in [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese")'s _[The Aviator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Aviator\_(2004\_film) "The Aviator (2004 film)")_ in 2004. Scorsese, whose daughter was a No Doubt fan, showed reciprocal interest in casting Stefani after seeing her picture from a [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe")-inspired photo shoot for _[Teen Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen\_Vogue "Teen Vogue")_ in 2003.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-54) To prepare for the role, Stefani read two biographies and watched 18 of Harlow's films.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) Shooting her part took four to five days, and Stefani had few lines.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-55) Stefani lent her voice to the title character of the 2004 video game _[Malice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malice\_(2004\_video\_game) "Malice (2004 video game)")_, but the company opted not to use No Doubt band members' voices.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-56)

### 2006–2013: _The Sweet Escape_ and return to No Doubt

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2006–2013: The Sweet Escape and return to No Doubt")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/GwenStefaniJonesBeach.jpg/250px-GwenStefaniJonesBeach.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GwenStefaniJonesBeach.jpg)

Stefani performing "[Wind It Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_It_Up_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Wind It Up (Gwen Stefani song)")" during [The Sweet Escape Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweet_Escape_Tour "The Sweet Escape Tour") in 2007

Stefani's second studio album, _[The Sweet Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sweet\_Escape "The Sweet Escape")_, was released on December 1, 2006.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-Sweet_Escape_release-57) Stefani continued working with Kanal, Perry, and [the Neptunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Neptunes "The Neptunes"), along with [Akon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akon "Akon") and [Tim Rice-Oxley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Rice-Oxley "Tim Rice-Oxley") from English rock band [Keane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keane_(band) "Keane (band)"). The album focuses more heavily on [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") and [dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music") for [clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightclub "Nightclub") than its predecessor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-parents-18) Its release coincided with the DVD release of Stefani's first [tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_tour "Concert tour"), entitled _[Harajuku Lovers Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku\_Lovers\_Live "Harajuku Lovers Live")_. [Sia Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia_Michel "Sia Michel") wrote that it "has a surprisingly moody, lightly autobiographical feel... but Stefani isn't convincing as a dissatisfied [diva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diva "Diva")"[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-58) and [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") called the album a "hasty return" that repeats _Love. Angel. Music. Baby._ with less energy.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-59)

"[Wind It Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_It_Up_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Wind It Up (Gwen Stefani song)")", the album's [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single"), used [yodeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yodeling "Yodeling") and an [interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation_(popular_music) "Interpolation (popular music)") of _[The Sound of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sound\_of\_Music\_(film) "The Sound of Music (film)")_,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-60) and peaked in the top 10 in the US and the UK.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-61) The [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweet_Escape_(song) "The Sweet Escape (song)") reached the top 10 in over 15 nations, including number two peaks in the US, Australia and the UK. To promote _The Sweet Escape_, Stefani was a mentor on the [sixth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Idol_(season_6) "American Idol (season 6)") of _[American Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Idol "American Idol")_ and performed the song with Akon. The song earned her a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_Grammy_Awards "50th Grammy Awards") nomination for [Best Pop Collaboration with Vocals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Collaboration_with_Vocals "Best Pop Collaboration with Vocals").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-62) Three more singles were released from the album; "[4 in the Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_in_the_Morning "4 in the Morning")", "[Now That You Got It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Now_That_You_Got_It "Now That You Got It")" which featured [Damian Marley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damian_Marley "Damian Marley") and "[Early Winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Winter "Early Winter")". To promote the album, Stefani embarked on a worldwide tour, [The Sweet Escape Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweet_Escape_Tour "The Sweet Escape Tour"), which covered North America, Europe, Asia and the Pacific and part of Latin America. In an interview with _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ on June 6, 2011, Stefani stated that she had no plans to continue work as a solo artist.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-63)

With Stefani promoting _The Sweet Escape_, No Doubt began work on a new album without her[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-64) and planned to complete it after Stefani's Sweet Escape Tour was finished.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-65) In March 2008, the band started making posts concerning the progression of the album on their official fan forum. Stefani made a post on March 28, 2008, stating that songwriting had commenced but was slow on her end because she was pregnant with her second child.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-66)_The Singles 1992–2003_ became available on December 9, 2008, for the video game _[Rock Band 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_Band\_2 "Rock Band 2")_.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-67) Adrian Young played drums on [Scott Weiland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Weiland "Scott Weiland")'s album _["Happy" in Galoshes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Happy%22\_in\_Galoshes "\"Happy\" in Galoshes")_. No Doubt headlined the [Bamboozle 2009 festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bamboozle "The Bamboozle") in May 2009, along with [Fall Out Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_Out_Boy "Fall Out Boy"). The band completed a [national tour in mid-2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Tour_2009_(No_Doubt) "Summer Tour 2009 (No Doubt)").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-68)

The new album _[Push and Shove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push\_and\_Shove\_(album) "Push and Shove (album)")_ was released on September 25, preceded by the first single, "[Settle Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settle_Down_(No_Doubt_song) "Settle Down (No Doubt song)")", on July 16. The music video for "Settle Down" was directed by [Sophie Muller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Muller "Sophie Muller") (who has previously directed numerous music videos for No Doubt). Also around this time No Doubt were guest mentors for the UK version of _The X-Factor_.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-69) "Settle Down" peaked at 34 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 with the album peaking at number three on the US _Billboard_ 200. On November 3, 2012, the band pulled its music video "[Looking Hot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looking_Hot "Looking Hot")" from the Internet after receiving complaints that it was insensitive towards Native Americans.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-70) In January 2013, No Doubt make a cameo appearance in a hot air ballon for the [third season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portlandia_(season_3) "Portlandia (season 3)") of _[Portlandia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portlandia\_(TV\_series) "Portlandia (TV series)")_.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-71)

Stefani in 2014

On April 12, 2014, Stefani made a surprise appearance at the [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival") festival, where she joined [Pharrell Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharrell_Williams "Pharrell Williams") onstage during his set to perform "Hollaback Girl".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-72) On April 29, it was officially confirmed that Stefani would join the [seventh season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_(American_TV_series)_season_7 "The Voice (American TV series) season 7") of _[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Voice\_(U.S.\_TV\_series) couldn't due to her pregnancy.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-73) Nine years after the previous time, she attended the [2014 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2014 MTV Video Music Awards").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-74) Stefani appears as a featured artist on [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5")'s song "[My Heart Is Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Heart_Is_Open "My Heart Is Open")", co-written by [Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia"), from the band's album _[V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V\_(Maroon\_5\_album) "V (Maroon 5 album)")_,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-75) which was performed for the first time with [Adam Levine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Levine "Adam Levine") and an orchestra at the [2015 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Grammy_Awards "2015 Grammy Awards").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-76) Stefani also collaborated with [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") on the track "Together" from his album _[Motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion\_(Calvin\_Harris\_album) "Motion (Calvin Harris album)")_.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-77)

On September 8, 2014, Stefani told [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News "MTV News") during [New York Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Fashion_Week "New York Fashion Week") that she was working on both a No Doubt album and a solo album, and that she was working with Williams.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-78) Stefani released her comeback single "[Baby Don't Lie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Don't_Lie "Baby Don't Lie")" on October 20, 2014, co-written with producers [Ryan Tedder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tedder "Ryan Tedder"), [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco"), and [Noel Zancanella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noel_Zancanella "Noel Zancanella").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-79)_Billboard_ announced that her third studio album was set to be released in December with [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") serving as executive producer.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-80) In late October, "[Spark the Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spark_the_Fire "Spark the Fire")", a new track from Stefani's third album, was released. The song was produced by [Pharrell Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharrell_Williams "Pharrell Williams").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-81) On November 23, the full song premiered online.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-82)[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving\_a\_source "Help:Archiving a source")_] Both "Baby Don't Lie" and "Spark the Fire" were later scrapped from Stefani's third album. On January 13, 2015, Stefani and Williams also recorded a song titled "[Shine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shine_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "Shine (Gwen Stefani song)")", for the _[Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_(film) "Paddington (film)")_ soundtrack. Stefani and Sia worked together on a ballad, called "Start a War" which was expected to be released on Stefani's third studio album as well, but it was not included on the final cut.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-83) On July 10, 2015, American rapper [Eminem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminem "Eminem") featured Stefani on his single "[Kings Never Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_Never_Die "Kings Never Die")", from the _[Southpaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southpaw\_(film) "Southpaw (film)")_ film soundtrack. ## Other ventures

Stefani made most of the clothing that she wore on stage with No Doubt, resulting in increasingly eclectic combinations. Stylist [Andrea Lieberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Lieberman "Andrea Lieberman") introduced her to [haute couture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_couture "Haute couture") clothing, which led to Stefani launching a fashion line named [L.A.M.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.M.B. "L.A.M.B.") in 2004.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) The line takes influence from a variety of fashions, including Guatemalan, [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_street_fashion "Japanese street fashion"), and Jamaican styles.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-150) The line achieved popularity among celebrities and is worn by stars such as [Teri Hatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teri_Hatcher "Teri Hatcher"), [Nicole Kidman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Kidman "Nicole Kidman"), and Stefani herself.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-sundaytelegraph-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-152) In June 2005, she expanded her collection with the less expensive Harajuku Lovers line, which she referred to as "a glorified merchandise line", with varied products including a camera, [mobile phone charms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_phone_charm "Mobile phone charm"), and undergarments.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-153)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-radiation-154) In late 2006, Stefani released a limited edition line of dolls called "Love. Angel. Music. Baby. Fashion dolls". The dolls are inspired by the clothes Stefani and the Harajuku Girls wore while touring for the album.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-155)

There are five different fragrances based on the four Harajuku Girls and Stefani herself called Love, Lil' Angel, Music, Baby and G (Gwen).[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-157)As of January 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit), Stefani has become the spokesperson for [L'Oréal Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Or%C3%A9al "L'Oréal").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-158) In 2016, [Urban Decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Decay_(cosmetics) "Urban Decay (cosmetics)") released a limited edition cosmetic collection in collaboration with Stefani.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-159) After needing to wear glasses, she began designing eyewear.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-160) In 2016, Gwen began releasing eyewear under her fashion label L.A.M.B.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-161) She also began releasing affordable eyewear under the label GX, with Tura Inc.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-162)

In 2014, Stefani announced the production of an animated series about her and the Harajuku Girls.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-Kuu_Kuu_reveal-163) Along with Vision Animation and Moody Street Kids,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-164) Stefani has helped create the show which features herself, Love, Angel, Music, and Baby as the band, HJ5, who fight evil whilst trying to pursue their music career.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-165) Mattel was the global toy licensee and the series itself, _[Kuu Kuu Harajuku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuu\_Kuu\_Harajuku "Kuu Kuu Harajuku")_ was distributed worldwide by [DHX Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DHX_Media "DHX Media").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-166)

In 2018, Stefani had reportedly filed to trademark P8NT for a potential line of "make-up, skincare, fragrance and hair dyes",[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-167) and in March 2022, she launched a makeup brand called GXVE Beauty.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-169)

## Public image

[![Image 12: Color picture of singer Gwen Stefani performing](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/GwenStefaniTheRealThing.jpg/250px-GwenStefaniTheRealThing.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GwenStefaniTheRealThing.jpg)

Stefani performing "[The Real Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Real_Thing_(Gwen_Stefani_song) "The Real Thing (Gwen Stefani song)")" during the [Harajuku Lovers Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku_Lovers_Tour "Harajuku Lovers Tour") in 2005

Stefani began wearing a [bindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bindi_(decoration) "Bindi (decoration)") in the mid-1990s after attending several family gatherings with [Tony Kanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Kanal "Tony Kanal"), who is of Indian heritage.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-191) During No Doubt's breakthrough, she wore the forehead decoration in several of the band's music videos and briefly popularized it as an accessory.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-ew-192) Since the 1995 music video for "Just a Girl", Stefani has been known for her midriff and frequently wears tops that expose it.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-193) Her makeup design generally includes light face powder, bright red lipstick, and arched eyebrows; she wrote about the subject in the song "Magic's in the Makeup" on the album _Return of Saturn_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-vogue-16) Stefani is a natural brunette, but her hair has not been its natural color since she was in ninth grade.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-194) Since late 1994, she has usually had platinum blonde hair. Stefani discussed this in the song "Platinum Blonde Life" on _Rock Steady_ and played original blonde bombshell [Jean Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Harlow "Jean Harlow") in the 2004 biopic _[The Aviator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Aviator\_(2004\_film) "The Aviator (2004 film)")_.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-195) She dyed her hair blue in 1998[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-ew-192) and pink in 1999; she appeared on the cover of _Return of Saturn_ with pink hair.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-196)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-197)

In 2006, Stefani modified her image, inspired by that of [Michelle Pfeiffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Pfeiffer "Michelle Pfeiffer")'s character [Elvira Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvira_Hancock "Elvira Hancock") in the 1983 film _[Scarface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarface\_(1983\_film) "Scarface (1983 film)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-hb-9) The reinvented image included a symbol consisting of two back-to-back 'G's, which appears on a diamond-encrusted key she wears on a necklace and which became a motif in the promotion of _The Sweet Escape_.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-radiation-154) Stefani raised concerns in January 2007 about her rapid [weight loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weight_loss "Weight loss") following her pregnancy. She later stated that she had been on a diet since the [sixth grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_grade "Sixth grade") to fit in size 4 clothing.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-198) A wax figure of Stefani was unveiled at [Madame Tussauds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds") Las Vegas at [The Venetian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Venetian,_Las_Vegas "The Venetian, Las Vegas") on September 22, 2010.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-199) The release of Stefani's first solo album brought attention to her entourage of four [Harajuku Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku_Girls "Harajuku Girls"), who appear in outfits influenced by [Gothic Lolita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_Lolita "Gothic Lolita") fashion,[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-200) and are named for the area around the [Harajuku Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku_Station "Harajuku Station") of [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"). Stefani's clothing also took influence from Japanese fashion, in a style described as a combination between [Christian Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Dior "Christian Dior") and Japan.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-guardian-47) The dancers are featured in her music videos, press coverage, and on the album cover for _Love. Angel. Music. Baby._, with a song named for and dedicated to them on the album. They were also featured in, and the namesake for, Stefani's [Harajuku Lovers Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harajuku_Lovers_Tour "Harajuku Lovers Tour"). _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes\_(magazine) "Forbes (magazine)")_ magazine reported that Stefani earned $27 million between June 2007 to June 2008 for her tour, fashion line and commercials, making her the world's 10th highest paid music personality at the time.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-201)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gwen_Stefani&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Following the [2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_T%C5%8Dhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami"), Stefani donated $1 million to [Save the Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Children "Save the Children")'s Japan Earthquake–Tsunami Children in Emergency Fund.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-236) Stefani also ran an auction on [eBay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBay "EBay") from April 11 to 25, 2011, allowing participants to bid on vintage clothing items from her personal wardrobe and custom T-shirts designed and signed by her, as well as an admission to a private Harajuku-themed tea party hosted by her on June 7, 2011, at Los Angeles' first Japanese-style [maid café](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maid_caf%C3%A9 "Maid café") and [pop art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_art "Pop art") space, Royal/T, with proceeds from the auction going to Save the Children's relief effort.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-237)[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-238)

At the [amfAR gala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AmfAR_gala "AmfAR gala") during the [2011 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Cannes_Film_Festival "2011 Cannes Film Festival"), Stefani auctioned off the lacy black dress she wore at the event for charity, raising over $125,000.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-nymag-239) A representative for designer Michael Angel, who helped Stefani with the design and worked as a stylist, said that Angel created the gown, not Stefani.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-nymag-239)[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-240) In response, Angel released a statement confirming that the dress was designed by Stefani for L.A.M.B. to wear and be auctioned off at the amfAR gala.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-241) Stefani hosted a fundraiser with [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_the_United_States "First Lady of the United States")[Michelle Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama "Michelle Obama") in August 2012 at the singer's [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") home.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani#cite_note-242)

**Shawn Peter Raul Mendes** ([/ˈ m ɛ n d ɛ z/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_MEN-dez_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), European Portuguese:[[ˈmẽdɨʃ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese"); born August 8, 1998) is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and musician. Mendes gained early recognition for posting popular song covers on the social media platforms [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") and [Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) "Vine (service)"). He later signed to [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") and released his [self-titled debut EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shawn_Mendes_EP "The Shawn Mendes EP") in 2014.

Mendes's debut studio album, _[Handwritten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handwritten\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Handwritten (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2015), debuted atop the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and featured his breakout single "[Stitches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stitches_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Stitches (Shawn Mendes song)")", which reached number one in the UK and the top 10 in the US and Canada. His second studio album, _[Illuminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2016), produced a string of successful singles, including "[Treat You Better](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treat_You_Better_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Treat You Better (Shawn Mendes song)")", "[Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Mercy (Shawn Mendes song)")", and "[There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There's_Nothing_Holdin'_Me_Back "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back")". His [self-titled third studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)") featured the lead single "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")", while its deluxe edition included the hit singles "[If I Can't Have You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Can't_Have_You_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "If I Can't Have You (Shawn Mendes song)")" and "[Señorita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1orita_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Camila_Cabello_song) "Señorita (Shawn Mendes and Camila Cabello song)")"; the latter became his first US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one single. His fourth studio album, _[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2020), made him the youngest male artist ever to top the _Billboard_ 200 with four studio albums.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-1) After a brief hiatus, Mendes released his [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music")-driven fifth studio album, [_Shawn_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_(album) "Shawn (album)") (2024).

[Mendes's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Shawn_Mendes "List of awards and nominations received by Shawn Mendes") include thirteen [SOCAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Music_Publishers_of_Canada "Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada") awards, ten [MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award "MTV Europe Music Award"), eight [Juno Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Award "Juno Award"), eight [iHeartRadio MMVAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_MMVAs "IHeartRadio MMVAs"), two [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), in addition to nominations for three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") and a [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award"). In 2018, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world on their [annual list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").

## Early life

Shawn Peter Raul Mendes was born on August 8, 1998, in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), to English mother Karen (née Rayment) and Portuguese father Manuel Mendes, and was raised in [Pickering, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickering,_Ontario "Pickering, Ontario").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-2) His mother is a real estate agent, while his father is a businessman from the [Algarve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algarve "Algarve") who sells bar and restaurant supplies in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-:1-3) He has a younger sister named Aaliyah.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-4) He was raised in a religious family,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-5) and played youth soccer with [Pickering FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickering_FC "Pickering FC").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-6) Mendes graduated from [Pine Ridge Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_Ridge_Secondary_School "Pine Ridge Secondary School") in June 2016,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-7) where he played ice hockey and soccer, joined his high school [glee club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glee_club "Glee club"), and crafted his stage presence in acting lessons (leading as [Prince Charming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Charming "Prince Charming") at one point). He also auditioned for the [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel") in Toronto.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-8)

## Career

### 2013–2015: _Handwritten_

Main article: [Handwritten (Shawn Mendes album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handwritten_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Handwritten (Shawn Mendes album)")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Shawn_Mendes_VOA.png/250px-Shawn_Mendes_VOA.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shawn_Mendes_VOA.png)

Mendes at the [Jingle Ball Tour 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle_Ball_Tour_2014 "Jingle Ball Tour 2014")

Mendes learned to play guitar by watching [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") tutorial videos at the age of 13 in 2012.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-9) Less than a year later he started posting [cover videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") on YouTube. Mendes started attracting viewers after he posted a cover from [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[As Long as You Love Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As_Long_as_You_Love_Me_(Justin_Bieber_song) "As Long as You Love Me (Justin Bieber song)")" on the social video app [Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) "Vine (service)") in 2013 and got 10,000 likes and as many followers the next day. After that he gained millions of views and followers in a few months, becoming well known for his six-second snippets of renditions of many popular songs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-10) Mendes saw Bieber as a career model at the time.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-11) By August 2014, he was the third most-followed musician on Vine.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-12) Artist manager Andrew Gertler discovered Mendes online in November 2013, bringing him to [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") in January 2014. In April, he won [Ryan Seacrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Seacrest "Ryan Seacrest")'s "Best Cover Song" contest with "[Say Something](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_Something_(A_Great_Big_World_song) "Say Something (A Great Big World song)")" by [A Great Big World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Great_Big_World "A Great Big World"). He officially signed to Island in May 2014.

He released his first single "[Life of the Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_of_the_Party_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Life of the Party (Shawn Mendes song)")" on June 26, 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Billboard-13) He became the youngest to debut in the top 25 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hot_100 "The Hot 100"), making it to number 24 for the week ending July 12, 2014.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Idolator1-14) Prior to his signing, Mendes toured as a member of the [Magcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magcon "Magcon") Tour[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-15) alongside other young Viners with a large following on social media.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-16) Mendes was also on a nationwide tour with [Austin Mahone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Mahone "Austin Mahone") as an opening act. He released his debut major label EP in July.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-17) The EP debuted and peaked at number five on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-18) selling 48,000 copies in its first week.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-19) He won a [Teen Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice "Teen Choice") award in 2014 for Webstar in Music.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-20) On September 5, 2014, "[Oh Cecilia (Breaking My Heart)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh_Cecilia_(Breaking_My_Heart) "Oh Cecilia (Breaking My Heart)")" featuring Mendes was released as the fifth single from [the Vamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Vamps_(British_band) "The Vamps (British band)")' debut album, _[Meet the Vamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_the\_Vamps "Meet the Vamps")_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-21) On November 6, 2014, "[Something Big](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_Big_(song) "Something Big (song)")" was released as the second single.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-22)

On April 14, 2015, Mendes released his full-length album _Handwritten_, which debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 chart with 119,000 [equivalent album units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Album_Sales "Top Album Sales"), selling 106,000 copies in its first week and was certified platinum.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) Mendes then became the youngest artist to debut at number one since the release of [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s _[My World 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_World\_2.0 "My World ### 2016–2017: _Illuminate_

Main article: [Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg/250px-Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg)

Mendes in 2017

On January 21, 2016, Mendes made his acting debut on [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW")'s _[The 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_(TV\_series) "The 100 (TV series)")_ third-season premiere.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-35) He later announced his second world tour as a headliner, the [Shawn Mendes World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_World_Tour "Shawn Mendes World Tour"), which started in March 2016[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-36) and sold out 38 shows in North America and Europe within minutes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-ABC-37)

Mendes released "[Treat You Better](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treat_You_Better_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Treat You Better (Shawn Mendes song)")", the lead single from his second studio album, in June 2016.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-38) In the US, the single reached the top 10 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, became his second single to peak atop both the Adult Contemporary[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) and Adult Pop Songs[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) chart, and was certified triple platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) It also went top 10 in the UK. The album, [_Illuminate_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)"), was released on September 23, 2016, and debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 with 145,000 equivalent album units, including 121,000 in pure album sales and was certified platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-US_debut-39) It debuted atop the charts in Canada, becoming his second number one album in his home country. "[Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Mercy (Shawn Mendes song)")" was released as the second single on August 18, 2016,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-40) which entered the top 20 in the US and the UK and was certified double platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) Mendes released the live album _Live at Madison Square Garden_ in December 2016.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-41) He appeared as the musical guest on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, December 3, 2016.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-SNL-42)

In April 2017, Mendes embarked on his [Illuminate World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_World_Tour "Illuminate World Tour"), which sold-out arenas around the world such as [Los Angeles'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles")[Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") and London's [The O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2_Arena "The O2 Arena").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-staples_center-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Standard-45) He released the single "[There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There's_Nothing_Holdin'_Me_Back "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back")" on April 20, 2017, included on his [_Illuminate_ deluxe edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-46) The song was Mendes's third single to reach the top 10 in the US[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Forbes-47) and third single to reach number one on both the Adult Contemporary[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) and Adult Pop Songs[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) chart.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-48) In August 2017, he became the first artist under 20 years old to have three number-one songs on the _Billboard_ Adult Pop Songs chart.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-49) In November 2017, Mendes became the first artist to have three number-one songs on the _Billboard_ Adult Contemporary chart before turning 20 years old,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) an unprecedented feat since the founding of the chart more than 50 years ago.

Mendes was listed among _Time's The 30 Most Influential Teens of 2016_[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Time_2016-50) and made his first appearance on _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")'s [30 Under 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes\_30\_Under\_30 "Forbes 30 Under 30") 2016: Music_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-51) He topped _Billboard_'s 21 Under 21 list in 2017, after his two albums topped the _Billboard_ 200 and his single "There's Nothing Holding Me Back" became his fifth top 20 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-52)

### 2018–2019: _Shawn Mendes_

Main article: [Shawn Mendes (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_(cropped).jpg)

Mendes performs "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")" at the [2018 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2018 MTV Video Music Awards").

On March 22, 2018, Mendes released the lead single "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")" from his upcoming third studio album,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-53) followed up by the second single "[Lost in Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_in_Japan "Lost in Japan")" on March 23.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-54) "In My Blood" topped the _Billboard_ Adult Pop Songs chart, making Mendes the first and only artist to have four number one singles in the chart before turning 20 years old.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) "[Youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Youth (Shawn Mendes song)")" was released on May 3, featuring American singer [Khalid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalid_(American_singer) "Khalid (American singer)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-55) His [self-titled studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)") was released on May 25, 2018, to positive critical reviews, with particular praise towards his songwriting and artistic growth.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-56) It debuted at number one in Canada, making it his third number one album in his home country. It debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200, making Mendes the third-youngest artist to collect three number-one albums.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-57)

To promote the album, Mendes embarked on his self-titled world tour in 2019.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-58) Besides the tour, he performed at music festivals across Europe, North America, and South America. He performed at a [televised concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen's_Birthday_Party "The Queen's Birthday Party") honouring the 92nd birthday of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") on April 21, 2018.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-59) He made TV show appearances on _[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Late\_Show\_with\_James\_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")_ in June where he sang one of his latest singles each night for a week.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-60) The tracks he performed live were "Nervous",[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-61) "Lost in Japan",[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-62) "Perfectly Wrong",[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-63) and the duet with Julia Michaels "Like to be You".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-64) Mendes made an appearance on the late-night talk show _The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon_ in October and performed Lost in Japan.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-65) He, together with Fallon and the show's resident band [The Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roots "The Roots"), performed a special version of "Treat You Better" for the show's _Classroom Instruments_ series.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-66) He has also performed his latest singles on the [iHeartRadio MMVAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_MMVAs "IHeartRadio MMVAs") in Canada on August 27, where he received eight nominations and won four awards.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-67)

Mendes starred in a documentary directed by YouTube star [Casey Neistat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Neistat "Casey Neistat"). The short film is part of YouTube's Artist Spotlight Story series, featuring an interview with Mendes and backstage and behind-the-scenes footage of Mendes during one of his tours.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-68) The trailer was released on YouTube on September 22 to officially announce the upcoming documentary.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-69) The documentary, _Shawn Mendes – Artist Spotlight Stories_, was published on September 28.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-70) Ahead of the official release day, Mendes and Neistat held a previewing show of the film where selected fans of Mendes were invited for the event.

The remixed version of "Lost in Japan", by Russian-German DJ [Zedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zedd "Zedd"), was released on September 27.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-71) Mendes performed the remix version of the single during the [American Music Awards of 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2018 "American Music Awards of 2018") held in Los Angeles on October 9.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-72) He was joined onstage by Zedd.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-73) Mendes was listed on _Billboard_ "21 Under 21 2018", topping the list for the second year in a row for his chart performance, having three consecutive number one albums.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-74)
