### 2020–2023: _Wonder_

Main article: [Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")

On September 30, 2020, Mendes announced that his fourth studio album, _[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")_, would be released on December 4, along with announcing that the album's lead single, also called "[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes song)")", would be released on October 2.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-89) Through promotional videos, "Intro", the first song from the album, was also released.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-90) "Wonder" debuted and peaked at number 18 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-91) On October 13, Mendes announced that a documentary titled _[Shawn Mendes: In Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_Mendes:\_In\_Wonder "Shawn Mendes: In Wonder")_, which chronicles the past few years of his life, would be released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on November 23.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-92) A concert film, titled _Shawn Mendes: Live in Concert_, was released on Netflix on November 25, following his first performance at the [Rogers Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Centre "Rogers Centre") on September 6, 2019.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-93)

On November 16, 2020, Mendes announced that the second single from _Wonder_ was a collaboration with [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber") on a track entitled "[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Justin_Bieber_song) "Monster (Shawn Mendes and Justin Bieber song)")".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-94) The single and the music video were released on November 20, 2020.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-95) The song peaked at number eight on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-96) Mendes performed "Monster" live for the first time with Bieber at the [2020 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2020 "American Music Awards of 2020"); he also performed "Wonder".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-97) On December 4, the album _Wonder_ was released, debuting at number one in the US as well as Canada.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-98) On December 6, Mendes held a concert event titled, _Wonder: The Experience_, where he did a Q&A session, performed songs from the album, and talked about the behind the scenes of making of the record.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-99) On December 7, Mendes did an interview alongside [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey") and performed "Dream" for the first time on television during his appearance on _[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Late\_Show\_with\_James\_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")_.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-100)

On August 20, 2021, Mendes released "[Summer of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_of_Love_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Tainy_song) "Summer of Love (Shawn Mendes and Tainy song)")" with [Tainy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tainy "Tainy").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-101) That same month, it was announced that Mendes would serve as an executive producer–via his production banner, Permanent Content–for Legendary's TV adaptation of [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix")'s video game _[Life Is Strange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_Is\_Strange "Life Is Strange")_.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-102) On September 23, 2021, Mendes announced that he would be embarking on [Wonder: The World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder:_The_World_Tour "Wonder: The World Tour"), across North America, the United Kingdom, and Europe, consisting of 64 dates and starting on March 14, 2022, at the [Royal Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Arena "Royal Arena") in Copenhagen.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-103) He performed seven shows before postponing three weeks due to his mental health before eventually canceling the remaining eighty scheduled shows.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-2022cancel-104) Mendes stated he would continue to make music and that he hopes to tour again.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-cancelTour2-105) On November 30, 2021, Mendes announced that a new single, titled "[It'll Be Okay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It'll_Be_Okay "It'll Be Okay")", would be released on December 1.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-106) On March 20, 2022, he premiered a new song titled "[When You're Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_You're_Gone_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "When You're Gone (Shawn Mendes song)")" during his performance at [SXSW 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-107)

Mendes voiced the title character in _[Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyle,\_Lyle,\_Crocodile\_(film) "Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile (film)")_, the movie adaptation of the children's book series by American author [Bernard Waber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Waber "Bernard Waber"), lending his pipes to a crocodile who only sings and never talks. The movie was released in the United States on October 7, 2022, by [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-108) An original song written and performed by Mendes, titled "Heartbeat," was released as the promotional single for the movie's [soundtrack album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyle,_Lyle,_Crocodile_(soundtrack) "Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile (soundtrack)") on September 23. On June 9, 2023, Mendes released "[What the Hell Are We Dying For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_the_Hell_Are_We_Dying_For%3F "What the Hell Are We Dying For?")" as a charity single. On November 21, "Witness Me" featuring Mendes, [Stormzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormzy "Stormzy"), and [Kirk Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Franklin "Kirk Franklin") was released as the fifth single from [Jacob Collier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Collier "Jacob Collier")'s album [Djesse Vol. 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djesse_Vol._4 "Djesse Vol. 4").

### 2024–present: _Shawn_

Main article: [Shawn (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_(album) "Shawn (album)")

In March 2024, Mendes announced his first solo live performance since canceling Wonder: The World Tour. Having made surprise guest appearances performing with [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), [Noah Kahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Kahan "Noah Kahan"), and [Niall Horan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niall_Horan "Niall Horan") since his hiatus, he announced he would be headlining the [Rock in Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_in_Rio "Rock in Rio") festival by himself on September 22. In the same post, he also announced that he was working on his fifth studio album. On July 31, he revealed the album's title, _[Shawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_(album) "Shawn (album)")_, and its release date: October 18, 2024 (later postponed to November 15). Two singles from the album, "[Why Why Why](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Why_Why_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Why Why Why (Shawn Mendes song)")" and "Isn't That Enough", were released on August 8.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-110) The third single off the record, "[Nobody Knows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody_Knows_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Nobody Knows (Shawn Mendes song)")", was released on September 12.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-111) The fourth single, "[Heart of Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_of_Gold_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Heart of Gold (Shawn Mendes song)")", was released on November 1.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-112)

To promote _Shawn_, Mendes embarked on an intimate concert tour of theatre shows throughout the places he recorded the album.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-113) Its selected venues hold between 2,000 and 3,000 attendees.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-114) The concerts started in [Woodstock, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_New_York "Woodstock, New York") on August 8, 2024, and concluded in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") on April 8, 2025.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-116) A [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film"), titled _[Shawn Mendes: For Friends and Family Only (A Live Concert Film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_Mendes:\_For\_Friends\_and\_Family\_Only\_(A\_Live\_Concert\_Film) "Shawn Mendes: For Friends and Family Only (A Live Concert Film)")_, premiered on November 14 in selected theaters.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-117)

On May 29, 2025, Mendes announced the [On the Road Again Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Road_Again_Tour_(Shawn_Mendes) "On the Road Again Tour (Shawn Mendes)"). The tour commenced on August 2, 2025, in Kosovo, and concluded on October 17.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-120)

## Artistry and musical influences

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/JohnMayerin2019.jpg/250px-JohnMayerin2019.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JohnMayerin2019.jpg)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg/250px-Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg)

Mendes cites [John Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mayer "John Mayer") and [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") as some of his musical influences.

Mendes has mainly been described as a pop and [folk-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk-pop "Folk-pop") singer.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-AllMusic-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-rsilluminate-122) Mendes has cited [John Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mayer "John Mayer"), Ed Sheeran, [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake"), and [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars") as his main musical influences.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-et_can-125) Growing up, Mendes listened to reggae music, [Led Zeppelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Led_Zeppelin "Led Zeppelin"), [Aerosmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerosmith "Aerosmith"), [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks"), and country music thanks to his parents.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-127) He expressed that his second studio album was influenced by Mayer's work[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-et_can-125) while his third album was inspired by Timberlake, [Kings of Leon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_of_Leon "Kings of Leon"), [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"), and [Daniel Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Caesar "Daniel Caesar").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-128) For Brittany Spanos of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, Mendes incorporates "catchy acoustic folk-pop tunes" in his catalogue,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-rsilluminate-122) while for Joe Coscarelli of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, "his soft, sometimes soulful pop-rock plays primarily to tweens and teenagers, but has also found traction on adult contemporary radio stations".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-tnyt-129) In an interview with [_Clash_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_(magazine) "Clash (magazine)"), Mendes stated:

> "I want to create anthems for people. I want to create anthems for big moments in their lives...I don't want my music to play for a few months and then go away forever. And not only that, I want to do incredible things that make a difference too. I think it's not only about the music you release, it's about the things you do while you're making the music."[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Clash-130)

## Brand endorsement and modelling

Mendes signed with [Wilhelmina Models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelmina_Models "Wilhelmina Models") in 2016.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Shawn_Mendes-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-134)

In June 2017, Mendes walked the runway during the "[Emporio Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armani "Armani") Spring 2018" show held in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-135) Mendes was wearing the Italian brand's new smartwatch, EA Connected, during the show. Ahead of his runway walk, the promotional video featuring Mendes was shown.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-136) In August 2017, Mendes launched his first fragrance, Shawn Mendes Signature, a fragrance for women and men.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-137) He launched his second fragrance, Shawn Signature II, also made for both men and women in August 2018.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-138)

On June 6, 2018, Mendes was announced as the ambassador for Emporio Armani's entire "Fall Winter 2018-2019" watch collection. In July 2018, photographs of Mendes wearing the new EA Connected smartwatches were published on social media.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-139)

On February 16, 2019, Mendes announced that he was the latest brand ambassador for [Calvin Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Klein_(fashion_house) "Calvin Klein (fashion house)")'s #MyCalvins campaign.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-140) During the [61st Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards"), [SmileDirectClub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmileDirectClub "SmileDirectClub") released an advertisement showcasing a campaign between the company and Mendes with some of the proceeds going to "organizations that seek to improve children's health as well as mental and emotional well-being."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-141) Later that month, Emporio Armani released a new black-and-white advertisement for its touchscreen smartwatches featuring an instrumental version of "In My Blood" with Mendes boxing.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-142)

In August 2019, Mendes announced a partnership with Canadian-based food chain [Tim Hortons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Hortons "Tim Hortons") in which he features in a commercial and on beverage cups,[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-143) followed by a partnership with [Roots Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roots_Canada "Roots Canada") in September.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-144) In February 2023, Mendes has been unveiled as the latest brand ambassador for America's luxury jewelry brand [David Yurman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yurman "David Yurman"), appearing alongside actress [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson") in the brand's 2023 campaign dubbed "Nature’s Artistry", inspired by nature and art.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-145)

In 2014, Mendes and [DoSomething.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoSomething.org "DoSomething.org") launched their campaign called "Notes from Shawn" where fans were encouraged to write positive notes and leave them in unexpected places. The campaign was inspired by the lyrics to his first single, "Life of the Party", and addressed low self-esteem, depression, and awareness of self-harm.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-146) They relaunched their campaign for the second year in a row in 2015, where the campaign was hashtagged online as NotesFromShawn. He partnered with BlendApp with the goal of raising up to $25,000, where $1 was raised for every signup and positive message shared on the application.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-147) The campaign was relaunched for a third year in a row in 2016.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-148)

He has also worked with [Pencils of Promise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pencils_of_Promise "Pencils of Promise"), a non-profit organization that builds schools and helps raise the quality of education for developing countries, raising $25,000 to build a school in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-149)

In September 2017, after witnessing the devastation of the [earthquake in Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Mexico_earthquake "Central Mexico earthquake"), Mendes created the Mexico Earthquake Relief Fund in conjunction with the [American Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Red_Cross "American Red Cross") and donated $100,000 towards relief efforts.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-150)

In 2018, Mendes worked with [Omaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaze "Omaze") to raise funds through donations to support the WE Schools program, a movement aiming to support youth through educational services and mentorship. Mendes encouraged his fans to help the cause while giving the donors a chance to attend his upcoming concert tour.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-151)

In September 2018, Mendes took part in the annual [Global Citizen Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Citizen_Festival "Global Citizen Festival") held at [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-152) He performed, alongside other artists such as Janelle Monáe, John Legend, and Janet Jackson, and raised awareness regarding the importance of education and children's lack of access to education around the world, particularly young women. Ahead of the event, he took to social media to reach out to Canada's Prime Minister [Justin Trudeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Trudeau "Justin Trudeau"), thanking the Prime Minister for leading the initiative for Leave No Girl Behind, a movement whose goal is to empower girls through workshops and programs,[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-153) and expressing his willingness to talk more about the project. He also encouraged his fans to support the movement. In response, the Prime Minister thanked Mendes and stated "The more people we have fighting for girls' education, the better! Let's talk."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-154)

In October 2018, Mendes, together with producer Teddy Geiger, released a cover of "[Under Pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Pressure "Under Pressure")" by the British rock band [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)") and [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-155) The single was part of a series of covers of Queen's songs, released in celebration of Queen's biopic _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-156) The proceeds from the single were donated to the [Mercury Phoenix Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Phoenix_Trust "Mercury Phoenix Trust"), an organization founded by Queen bandmembers after [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury")'s death, which helps fight against [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS").[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-157) Queen's manager, Jim Beach, expressed his gratitude to Mendes and Universal Music Group for helping the cause.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-158) On October 20, 2018, Mendes performed along with other artists such as Khalid, NF, Marshmello, Meghan Trainor, and Ella Mai at The [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") in Los Angeles for the "We Can Survive" event. The event was organized to raise funds for [Young Survival Coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Survival_Coalition "Young Survival Coalition"), in an effort to support young women who were diagnosed with [breast cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_cancer "Breast cancer").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-159)

In August 2019, Mendes announced the launch of the Shawn Mendes Foundation, aiming to "inspire and empower his fans and today's youth to bring about positive change in the world and advocate for issues they care most about."[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-160)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-161) On January 8, 2020, Mendes announced that both he and his Shawn Mendes Foundation would be donating an undisclosed sum of money to causes including the [Australian Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Red_Cross "Australian Red Cross"), the [New South Wales Rural Fire Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_Rural_Fire_Service "New South Wales Rural Fire Service"), and [South Australian Country Fire Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australian_Country_Fire_Service "South Australian Country Fire Service") to help ease the strain on those impacted by the devastating fires tearing through parts of the country.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-162) In March 2020 Mendes and The Shawn Mendes Foundation donated $175,000 to support COVID-19 relief to Toronto's SickKids Foundation, the largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care in Canada.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-163) Mendes and the Shawn Mendes Foundation announced Wonder Grants in December 2020 and have partnered with [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") to award the first set of Wonder Grants to young changemakers around the world. Wonder Grants aim to support and empower young creatives launching their projects across various fields, including music, film, education, science, environment, and technology.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-164) In January 2021, American chain of fast-casual restaurants [Chipotle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chipotle_Mexican_Grill "Chipotle Mexican Grill") announced its partnering with Mendes and his foundation to launch "Wonder Grants" supporting young innovators in sustainability, as well as a "Shawn Mendes Bowl" on the Chipotle app and Chipotle website for a limited time in the US and Canada. For every Shawn Mendes Bowl sold, Chipotle will donate $1 toward the foundation in support of changemakers and this marks the first time Chipotle has launched a philanthropic entrée on its menu.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-165) In June 2023, Mendes announced he collaborated with America luxury jewelry brand [David Yurman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yurman "David Yurman") and helped to design a woven hemp bracelet to benefit his foundation after previously announced as brand ambassador for the brand earlier this year. As part of the collaboration, 20% of the purchase price from the David Yurman bracelet will go to the foundation.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-166) Mendes has partnered with American subscription streaming service [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") as a tour sponsor for his [Wonder tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder:_The_World_Tour "Wonder: The World Tour") by visiting children's hospitals in the US. Mendes also planned to donate one dollar per ticket sold in North America towards his foundation's "Wonder Grants" program, which he would award to one "youth changemaker" in every city the tour visited.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-167)

In March 2020, Mendes participated in [iHeart Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeart_Media "IHeart Media")'s [Living Room Concert for America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeart_Living_Room_Concert_for_America "IHeart Living Room Concert for America"), a benefit to raise awareness and funds for the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-168) In March and April 2020, Mendes participated in Global Citizen Festival's Together at Home virtual concert to raise awareness and funds for the COVID-19 pandemic.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-169)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-170)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-171) Mendes has shown support for the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement. In May 2020 he, alongside [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello"), joined protests in Miami for racial justice after the [murder of George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd"), and has lent his [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") to raise the voice of Black activists.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-172)

On April 22, 2021, Mendes hosted a [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") video conference with the crew of [Expedition 65](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_65 "Expedition 65") on board the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"). The televised event covered a Q&A with students and children about various topics related to [Earth Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_Day "Earth Day"), such as climate change, Earth observations, and general physics, as well as the astronauts' experience on the space station.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-173)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-175) In June 2021, Mendes, along with several other celebrities, signed an open letter to the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"), urging lawmakers to pass the [Equality Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equality_Act_(United_States) "Equality Act (United States)"). The artists, including Mendes, said of the Act that it would "protect ... the most marginalized communities".[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-176)

In May 2021, Mendes joined Cabello and [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") actors to help fight the [COVID-19 pandemic in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India "COVID-19 pandemic in India") during its peak of cases. Mendes donated $50,000 through the organization _Give India_.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-177)

## Personal life

Mendes resides in [downtown Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Toronto "Downtown Toronto").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-178) He began dating American singer [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello") in July 2019.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-179) Their relationship sparked controversy, as both were accused of attempting to start a relationship [for publicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publicity_stunt "Publicity stunt"),[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Capital_2019-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Bonner_2019-182) but Mendes insisted it was "definitely not a publicity stunt".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Elle-183) The couple announced their split in November 2021.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-184) Mendes briefly dated [Sabrina Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter "Sabrina Carpenter") in early 2023.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-185) Since late 2025, Mendes has been in a relationship with [Bruna Marquezine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruna_Marquezine "Bruna Marquezine"), a Brazilian model and actress.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-186)

Regarding speculations about his [sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation"), in June 2016, Mendes stated: "First of all, I'm not gay. Second of all, it shouldn't make a difference if I was or if I wasn't. The focus should be on the music and not my sexuality."[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-188)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-189)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-190) In late October 2024, he commented that he was "still figuring out" his sexuality.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-191)

Mendes has been open about his struggles with [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder"), which he disclosed publicly in his song "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")". He said, "I spoke to a therapist a couple of times. [...] Therapy is what works for you. Therapy is listening to music and running on the treadmill, therapy is going to dinner with your friends—it's something that distracts you, that helps you heal and so it just depends on what you think therapy is. I made a conscious effort to be more connected to the people in my life. I found I was closing myself off from everybody, thinking that would help me battle it then realizing the only way I was going to battle it was completely opening up and letting people in."[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-192)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-193)

## Accolades and achievements

He won 18 [Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Music_Publishers_of_Canada "Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada") (SOCAN) awards, twelve [Juno Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Awards "Juno Awards"), eleven [MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "MTV Europe Music Awards") (EMA), eight [iHeartRadio Much Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_Much_Music_Video_Awards "IHeartRadio Much Music Video Awards") (MMVA), five [BMI Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMI_Awards "BMI Awards"), three [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), two [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and the Allan Slaight Honour from [Canada's Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada's_Walk_of_Fame "Canada's Walk of Fame"). He has been nominated for three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") and one [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards").

**Shawn Peter Raul Mendes** ([/ˈ m ɛ n d ɛ z/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_MEN-dez_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), European Portuguese:[[ˈmẽdɨʃ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese"); born August 8, 1998) is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and musician. Mendes gained early recognition for posting popular song covers on the social media platforms [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") and [Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) "Vine (service)"). He later signed to [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") and released his [self-titled debut EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shawn_Mendes_EP "The Shawn Mendes EP") in 2014.

Mendes's debut studio album, _[Handwritten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handwritten\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Handwritten (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2015), debuted atop the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and featured his breakout single "[Stitches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stitches_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Stitches (Shawn Mendes song)")", which reached number one in the UK and the top 10 in the US and Canada. His second studio album, _[Illuminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2016), produced a string of successful singles, including "[Treat You Better](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treat_You_Better_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Treat You Better (Shawn Mendes song)")", "[Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Mercy (Shawn Mendes song)")", and "[There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There's_Nothing_Holdin'_Me_Back "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back")". His [self-titled third studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)") featured the lead single "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")", while its deluxe edition included the hit singles "[If I Can't Have You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Can't_Have_You_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "If I Can't Have You (Shawn Mendes song)")" and "[Señorita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1orita_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Camila_Cabello_song) "Señorita (Shawn Mendes and Camila Cabello song)")"; the latter became his first US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one single. His fourth studio album, _[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")_ (2020), made him the youngest male artist ever to top the _Billboard_ 200 with four studio albums.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-1) After a brief hiatus, Mendes released his [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music")-driven fifth studio album, [_Shawn_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_(album) "Shawn (album)") (2024).

[Mendes's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Shawn_Mendes "List of awards and nominations received by Shawn Mendes") include thirteen [SOCAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Music_Publishers_of_Canada "Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada") awards, ten [MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award "MTV Europe Music Award"), eight [Juno Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Award "Juno Award"), eight [iHeartRadio MMVAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_MMVAs "IHeartRadio MMVAs"), two [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), in addition to nominations for three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") and a [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award"). In 2018, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world on their [annual list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").

## Early life

Shawn Peter Raul Mendes was born on August 8, 1998, in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), to English mother Karen (née Rayment) and Portuguese father Manuel Mendes, and was raised in [Pickering, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickering,_Ontario "Pickering, Ontario").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-2) His mother is a real estate agent, while his father is a businessman from the [Algarve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algarve "Algarve") who sells bar and restaurant supplies in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-:1-3) He has a younger sister named Aaliyah.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-4) He was raised in a religious family,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-5) and played youth soccer with [Pickering FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickering_FC "Pickering FC").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-6) Mendes graduated from [Pine Ridge Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_Ridge_Secondary_School "Pine Ridge Secondary School") in June 2016,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-7) where he played ice hockey and soccer, joined his high school [glee club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glee_club "Glee club"), and crafted his stage presence in acting lessons (leading as [Prince Charming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Charming "Prince Charming") at one point). He also auditioned for the [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel") in Toronto.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-8)

Mendes at the [Jingle Ball Tour 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle_Ball_Tour_2014 "Jingle Ball Tour 2014")

Mendes learned to play guitar by watching [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") tutorial videos at the age of 13 in 2012.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-9) Less than a year later he started posting [cover videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") on YouTube. Mendes started attracting viewers after he posted a cover from [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[As Long as You Love Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As_Long_as_You_Love_Me_(Justin_Bieber_song) "As Long as You Love Me (Justin Bieber song)")" on the social video app [Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) "Vine (service)") in 2013 and got 10,000 likes and as many followers the next day. After that he gained millions of views and followers in a few months, becoming well known for his six-second snippets of renditions of many popular songs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-10) Mendes saw Bieber as a career model at the time.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-11) By August 2014, he was the third most-followed musician on Vine.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-12) Artist manager Andrew Gertler discovered Mendes online in November 2013, bringing him to [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") in January 2014. In April, he won [Ryan Seacrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Seacrest "Ryan Seacrest")'s "Best Cover Song" contest with "[Say Something](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_Something_(A_Great_Big_World_song) "Say Something (A Great Big World song)")" by [A Great Big World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Great_Big_World "A Great Big World"). He officially signed to Island in May 2014.

He released his first single "[Life of the Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_of_the_Party_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Life of the Party (Shawn Mendes song)")" on June 26, 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Billboard-13) He became the youngest to debut in the top 25 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hot_100 "The Hot 100"), making it to number 24 for the week ending July 12, 2014.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Idolator1-14) Prior to his signing, Mendes toured as a member of the [Magcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magcon "Magcon") Tour[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-15) alongside other young Viners with a large following on social media.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-16) Mendes was also on a nationwide tour with [Austin Mahone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Mahone "Austin Mahone") as an opening act. He released his debut major label EP in July.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-17) The EP debuted and peaked at number five on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-18) selling 48,000 copies in its first week.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-19) He won a [Teen Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice "Teen Choice") award in 2014 for Webstar in Music.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-20) On September 5, 2014, "[Oh Cecilia (Breaking My Heart)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh_Cecilia_(Breaking_My_Heart) "Oh Cecilia (Breaking My Heart)")" featuring Mendes was released as the fifth single from [the Vamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Vamps_(British_band) "The Vamps (British band)")' debut album, _[Meet the Vamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_the\_Vamps "Meet the Vamps")_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-21) On November 6, 2014, "[Something Big](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_Big_(song) "Something Big (song)")" was released as the second single.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-22)

On April 14, 2015, Mendes released his full-length album _Handwritten_, which debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 chart with 119,000 [equivalent album units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Album_Sales "Top Album Sales"), selling 106,000 copies in its first week and was certified platinum.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) Mendes then became the youngest artist to debut at number one since the release of [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s _[My World 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_World\_2.0 "My World 2.0")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-idolator-25) The third single from the album, "[Stitches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stitches_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Stitches (Shawn Mendes song)")", peaked at number four on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100, becoming his first top 10 single in the US,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-26) and became his first number one on the Adult Pop Songs[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) and Adult Contemporary charts.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) The song later reached number one in the UK.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-29) Also in 2015, Mendes opened for [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") during [1989 World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_World_Tour "1989 World Tour") dates for North America and recorded "[Believe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believe_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Believe (Shawn Mendes song)")" for the soundtrack of [Disney Channel Original Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel_Original_Movie "Disney Channel Original Movie")_[Descendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descendants\_(2015\_film) "Descendants (2015 film)")_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-auto-31) In late 2015, Mendes and [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello"), who was at the time a member of the group [Fifth Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Harmony "Fifth Harmony"), released their collaborative single "[I Know What You Did Last Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Know_What_You_Did_Last_Summer_(song) "I Know What You Did Last Summer (song)")". The song was included on Mendes's _Handwritten Revisited_ reissue.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-32)

Mendes was listed among _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s "25 Most Influential Teens of 2014", debuting in the list after being the youngest-ever artist to debut in the top 25 of _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-33) He was listed in _Time_'s "The 30 Most Influential Teens of 2015", making the list after his debut album topped the _Billboard_ 200 and his single "Stitches" made the top 10 in the US and other countries.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-34)

### 2016–2017: _Illuminate_

Main article: [Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg/250px-Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shawn_Mendes_live_in_concert.jpg)

Mendes in 2017

On January 21, 2016, Mendes made his acting debut on [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW")'s _[The 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_(TV\_series) "The 100 (TV series)")_ third-season premiere.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-35) He later announced his second world tour as a headliner, the [Shawn Mendes World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_World_Tour "Shawn Mendes World Tour"), which started in March 2016[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-36) and sold out 38 shows in North America and Europe within minutes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-ABC-37)

Mendes released "[Treat You Better](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treat_You_Better_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Treat You Better (Shawn Mendes song)")", the lead single from his second studio album, in June 2016.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-38) In the US, the single reached the top 10 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, became his second single to peak atop both the Adult Contemporary[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) and Adult Pop Songs[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) chart, and was certified triple platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) It also went top 10 in the UK. The album, [_Illuminate_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)"), was released on September 23, 2016, and debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 with 145,000 equivalent album units, including 121,000 in pure album sales and was certified platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-US_debut-39) It debuted atop the charts in Canada, becoming his second number one album in his home country. "[Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Mercy (Shawn Mendes song)")" was released as the second single on August 18, 2016,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-40) which entered the top 20 in the US and the UK and was certified double platinum.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-RIAA-24) Mendes released the live album _Live at Madison Square Garden_ in December 2016.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-41) He appeared as the musical guest on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, December 3, 2016.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-SNL-42)

In April 2017, Mendes embarked on his [Illuminate World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_World_Tour "Illuminate World Tour"), which sold-out arenas around the world such as [Los Angeles'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles")[Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") and London's [The O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2_Arena "The O2 Arena").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-staples_center-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Standard-45) He released the single "[There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There's_Nothing_Holdin'_Me_Back "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back")" on April 20, 2017, included on his [_Illuminate_ deluxe edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-46) The song was Mendes's third single to reach the top 10 in the US[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Forbes-47) and third single to reach number one on both the Adult Contemporary[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) and Adult Pop Songs[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) chart.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-48) In August 2017, he became the first artist under 20 years old to have three number-one songs on the _Billboard_ Adult Pop Songs chart.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-49) In November 2017, Mendes became the first artist to have three number-one songs on the _Billboard_ Adult Contemporary chart before turning 20 years old,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-adultcontemporary-28) an unprecedented feat since the founding of the chart more than 50 years ago.

Mendes was listed among _Time's The 30 Most Influential Teens of 2016_[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Time_2016-50) and made his first appearance on _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")'s [30 Under 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes\_30\_Under\_30 "Forbes 30 Under 30") 2016: Music_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-51) He topped _Billboard_'s 21 Under 21 list in 2017, after his two albums topped the _Billboard_ 200 and his single "There's Nothing Holding Me Back" became his fifth top 20 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-52)

### 2018–2019: _Shawn Mendes_

Main article: [Shawn Mendes (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shawn_Mendes_Performs_%22In_My_Blood%22_MTV_VMAs_in_2018_Part_4_(cropped).jpg)

Mendes performs "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")" at the [2018 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2018 MTV Video Music Awards").

On March 22, 2018, Mendes released the lead single "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")" from his upcoming third studio album,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-53) followed up by the second single "[Lost in Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_in_Japan "Lost in Japan")" on March 23.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-54) "In My Blood" topped the _Billboard_ Adult Pop Songs chart, making Mendes the first and only artist to have four number one singles in the chart before turning 20 years old.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-popsongs-27) "[Youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Youth (Shawn Mendes song)")" was released on May 3, featuring American singer [Khalid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalid_(American_singer) "Khalid (American singer)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-55) His [self-titled studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes_(album) "Shawn Mendes (album)") was released on May 25, 2018, to positive critical reviews, with particular praise towards his songwriting and artistic growth.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-56) It debuted at number one in Canada, making it his third number one album in his home country. It debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200, making Mendes the third-youngest artist to collect three number-one albums.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-57)

To promote the album, Mendes embarked on his self-titled world tour in 2019.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-58) Besides the tour, he performed at music festivals across Europe, North America, and South America. He performed at a [televised concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen's_Birthday_Party "The Queen's Birthday Party") honouring the 92nd birthday of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") on April 21, 2018.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-59) He made TV show appearances on _[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Late\_Show\_with\_James\_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")_ in June where he sang one of his latest singles each night for a week.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-60) The tracks he performed live were "Nervous",[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-61) "Lost in Japan",[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-62) "Perfectly Wrong",[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-63) and the duet with Julia Michaels "Like to be You".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-64) Mendes made an appearance on the late-night talk show _The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon_ in October and performed Lost in Japan.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-65) He, together with Fallon and the show's resident band [The Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roots "The Roots"), performed a special version of "Treat You Better" for the show's _Classroom Instruments_ series.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-66) He has also performed his latest singles on the [iHeartRadio MMVAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_MMVAs "IHeartRadio MMVAs") in Canada on August 27, where he received eight nominations and won four awards.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-67)

Mendes starred in a documentary directed by YouTube star [Casey Neistat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Neistat "Casey Neistat"). The short film is part of YouTube's Artist Spotlight Story series, featuring an interview with Mendes and backstage and behind-the-scenes footage of Mendes during one of his tours.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-68) The trailer was released on YouTube on September 22 to officially announce the upcoming documentary.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-69) The documentary, _Shawn Mendes – Artist Spotlight Stories_, was published on September 28.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-70) Ahead of the official release day, Mendes and Neistat held a previewing show of the film where selected fans of Mendes were invited for the event.

The remixed version of "Lost in Japan", by Russian-German DJ [Zedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zedd "Zedd"), was released on September 27.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-71) Mendes performed the remix version of the single during the [American Music Awards of 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2018 "American Music Awards of 2018") held in Los Angeles on October 9.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-72) He was joined onstage by Zedd.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-73) Mendes was listed on _Billboard_ "21 Under 21 2018", topping the list for the second year in a row for his chart performance, having three consecutive number one albums.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-74)

video.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-78) The single debuted at number two in the US _Billboard_ Hot 100,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-:0-79) ### 2020–2023: _Wonder_

Main article: [Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_(Shawn_Mendes_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")

On September 30, 2020, Mendes announced that his fourth studio album, _[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_(Shawn\_Mendes\_album) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes album)")_, would be released on December 4, along with announcing that the album's lead single, also called "[Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Wonder (Shawn Mendes song)")", would be released on October 2.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-89) Through promotional videos, "Intro", the first song from the album, was also released.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-90) "Wonder" debuted and peaked at number 18 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-91) On October 13, Mendes announced that a documentary titled _[Shawn Mendes: In Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_Mendes:\_In\_Wonder "Shawn Mendes: In Wonder")_, which chronicles the past few years of his life, would be released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on November 23.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-92) A concert film, titled _Shawn Mendes: Live in Concert_, was released on Netflix on November 25, following his first performance at the [Rogers Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Centre "Rogers Centre") on September 6, 2019.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-93)

On November 16, 2020, Mendes announced that the second single from _Wonder_ was a collaboration with [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber") on a track entitled "[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Justin_Bieber_song) "Monster (Shawn Mendes and Justin Bieber song)")".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-94) The single and the music video were released on November 20, 2020.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-95) The song peaked at number eight on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-96) Mendes performed "Monster" live for the first time with Bieber at the [2020 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2020 "American Music Awards of 2020"); he also performed "Wonder".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-97) On December 4, the album _Wonder_ was released, debuting at number one in the US as well as Canada.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-98) On December 6, Mendes held a concert event titled, _Wonder: The Experience_, where he did a Q&A session, performed songs from the album, and talked about the behind the scenes of making of the record.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-99) On December 7, Mendes did an interview alongside [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey") and performed "Dream" for the first time on television during his appearance on _[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Late\_Show\_with\_James\_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")_.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-100)

On August 20, 2021, Mendes released "[Summer of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_of_Love_(Shawn_Mendes_and_Tainy_song) "Summer of Love (Shawn Mendes and Tainy song)")" with [Tainy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tainy "Tainy").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-101) That same month, it was announced that Mendes would serve as an executive producer–via his production banner, Permanent Content–for Legendary's TV adaptation of [Square Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_Enix "Square Enix")'s video game _[Life Is Strange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_Is\_Strange "Life Is Strange")_.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-102) On September 23, 2021, Mendes announced that he would be embarking on [Wonder: The World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder:_The_World_Tour "Wonder: The World Tour"), across North America, the United Kingdom, and Europe, consisting of 64 dates and starting on March 14, 2022, at the [Royal Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Arena "Royal Arena") in Copenhagen.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-103) He performed seven shows before postponing three weeks due to his mental health before eventually canceling the remaining eighty scheduled shows.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-2022cancel-104) Mendes stated he would continue to make music and that he hopes to tour again.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-cancelTour2-105) On November 30, 2021, Mendes announced that a new single, titled "[It'll Be Okay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It'll_Be_Okay "It'll Be Okay")", would be released on December 1.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-106) On March 20, 2022, he premiered a new song titled "[When You're Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_You're_Gone_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "When You're Gone (Shawn Mendes song)")" during his performance at [SXSW 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-107)

Mendes voiced the title character in _[Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyle,\_Lyle,\_Crocodile\_(film) "Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile (film)")_, the movie adaptation of the children's book series by American author [Bernard Waber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Waber "Bernard Waber"), lending his pipes to a crocodile who only sings and never talks. The movie was released in the United States on October 7, 2022, by [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-108) An original song written and performed by Mendes, titled "Heartbeat," was released as the promotional single for the movie's [soundtrack album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyle,_Lyle,_Crocodile_(soundtrack) "Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile (soundtrack)") on September 23. On June 9, 2023, Mendes released "[What the Hell Are We Dying For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_the_Hell_Are_We_Dying_For%3F "What the Hell Are We Dying For?")" as a charity single. On November 21, "Witness Me" featuring Mendes, [Stormzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormzy "Stormzy"), and [Kirk Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Franklin "Kirk Franklin") was released as the fifth single from [Jacob Collier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Collier "Jacob Collier")'s album [Djesse Vol. 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djesse_Vol._4 "Djesse Vol. 4").

### 2024–present: _Shawn_

Main article: [Shawn (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_(album) "Shawn (album)")

In March 2024, Mendes announced his first solo live performance since canceling Wonder: The World Tour. Having made surprise guest appearances performing with [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), [Noah Kahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Kahan "Noah Kahan"), and [Niall Horan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niall_Horan "Niall Horan") since his hiatus, he announced he would be headlining the [Rock in Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_in_Rio "Rock in Rio") festival by himself on September 22. In the same post, he also announced that he was working on his fifth studio album. On July 31, he revealed the album's title, _[Shawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_(album) "Shawn (album)")_, and its release date: October 18, 2024 (later postponed to November 15). Two singles from the album, "[Why Why Why](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Why_Why_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Why Why Why (Shawn Mendes song)")" and "Isn't That Enough", were released on August 8.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-110) The third single off the record, "[Nobody Knows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody_Knows_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Nobody Knows (Shawn Mendes song)")", was released on September 12.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-111) The fourth single, "[Heart of Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_of_Gold_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "Heart of Gold (Shawn Mendes song)")", was released on November 1.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-112)

To promote _Shawn_, Mendes embarked on an intimate concert tour of theatre shows throughout the places he recorded the album.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-113) Its selected venues hold between 2,000 and 3,000 attendees.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-114) The concerts started in [Woodstock, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_New_York "Woodstock, New York") on August 8, 2024, and concluded in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") on April 8, 2025.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-116) A [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film"), titled _[Shawn Mendes: For Friends and Family Only (A Live Concert Film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn\_Mendes:\_For\_Friends\_and\_Family\_Only\_(A\_Live\_Concert\_Film) "Shawn Mendes: For Friends and Family Only (A Live Concert Film)")_, premiered on November 14 in selected theaters.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-117)

On May 29, 2025, Mendes announced the [On the Road Again Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Road_Again_Tour_(Shawn_Mendes) "On the Road Again Tour (Shawn Mendes)"). The tour commenced on August 2, 2025, in Kosovo, and concluded on October 17.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-120)

## Artistry and musical influences

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/JohnMayerin2019.jpg/250px-JohnMayerin2019.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JohnMayerin2019.jpg)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg/250px-Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ed_Sheeran_2013.jpg)

Mendes cites [John Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mayer "John Mayer") and [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") as some of his musical influences.

Mendes has mainly been described as a pop and [folk-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk-pop "Folk-pop") singer.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-AllMusic-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-rsilluminate-122) Mendes has cited [John Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mayer "John Mayer"), Ed Sheeran, [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake"), and [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars") as his main musical influences.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-et_can-125) Growing up, Mendes listened to reggae music, [Led Zeppelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Led_Zeppelin "Led Zeppelin"), [Aerosmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerosmith "Aerosmith"), [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks"), and country music thanks to his parents.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-127) He expressed that his second studio album was influenced by Mayer's work[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-et_can-125) while his third album was inspired by Timberlake, [Kings of Leon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_of_Leon "Kings of Leon"), [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"), and [Daniel Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Caesar "Daniel Caesar").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-128) For Brittany Spanos of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, Mendes incorporates "catchy acoustic folk-pop tunes" in his catalogue,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-rsilluminate-122) while for Joe Coscarelli of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, "his soft, sometimes soulful pop-rock plays primarily to tweens and teenagers, but has also found traction on adult contemporary radio stations".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-tnyt-129) In an interview with [_Clash_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_(magazine) "Clash (magazine)"), Mendes stated:

> "I want to create anthems for people. I want to create anthems for big moments in their lives...I don't want my music to play for a few months and then go away forever. And not only that, I want to do incredible things that make a difference too. I think it's not only about the music you release, it's about the things you do while you're making the music."[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Clash-130)

## Brand endorsement and modelling

Mendes signed with [Wilhelmina Models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelmina_Models "Wilhelmina Models") in 2016.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Shawn_Mendes-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-134)

In June 2017, Mendes walked the runway during the "[Emporio Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armani "Armani") Spring 2018" show held in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-135) Mendes was wearing the Italian brand's new smartwatch, EA Connected, during the show. Ahead of his runway walk, the promotional video featuring Mendes was shown.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-136) In August 2017, Mendes launched his first fragrance, Shawn Mendes Signature, a fragrance for women and men.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-137) He launched his second fragrance, Shawn Signature II, also made for both men and women in August 2018.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-138)

On June 6, 2018, Mendes was announced as the ambassador for Emporio Armani's entire "Fall Winter 2018-2019" watch collection. In July 2018, photographs of Mendes wearing the new EA Connected smartwatches were published on social media.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-139)

On February 16, 2019, Mendes announced that he was the latest brand ambassador for [Calvin Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Klein_(fashion_house) "Calvin Klein (fashion house)")'s #MyCalvins campaign.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-140) During the [61st Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards"), [SmileDirectClub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmileDirectClub "SmileDirectClub") released an advertisement showcasing a campaign between the company and Mendes with some of the proceeds going to "organizations that seek to improve children's health as well as mental and emotional well-being."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-141) Later that month, Emporio Armani released a new black-and-white advertisement for its touchscreen smartwatches featuring an instrumental version of "In My Blood" with Mendes boxing.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-142)

In August 2019, Mendes announced a partnership with Canadian-based food chain [Tim Hortons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Hortons "Tim Hortons") in which he features in a commercial and on beverage cups,[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-143) followed by a partnership with [Roots Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roots_Canada "Roots Canada") in September.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-144) In February 2023, Mendes has been unveiled as the latest brand ambassador for America's luxury jewelry brand [David Yurman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yurman "David Yurman"), appearing alongside actress [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson") in the brand's 2023 campaign dubbed "Nature’s Artistry", inspired by nature and art.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-145)
