In 2014, Mendes and [DoSomething.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoSomething.org "DoSomething.org") launched their campaign called "Notes from Shawn" where fans were encouraged to write positive notes and leave them in unexpected places. The campaign was inspired by the lyrics to his first single, "Life of the Party", and addressed low self-esteem, depression, and awareness of self-harm.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-146) They relaunched their campaign for the second year in a row in 2015, where the campaign was hashtagged online as NotesFromShawn. He partnered with BlendApp with the goal of raising up to $25,000, where $1 was raised for every signup and positive message shared on the application.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-147) The campaign was relaunched for a third year in a row in 2016.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-148)

He has also worked with [Pencils of Promise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pencils_of_Promise "Pencils of Promise"), a non-profit organization that builds schools and helps raise the quality of education for developing countries, raising $25,000 to build a school in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-149)

In September 2017, after witnessing the devastation of the [earthquake in Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Mexico_earthquake "Central Mexico earthquake"), Mendes created the Mexico Earthquake Relief Fund in conjunction with the [American Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Red_Cross "American Red Cross") and donated $100,000 towards relief efforts.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-150)

In 2018, Mendes worked with [Omaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaze "Omaze") to raise funds through donations to support the WE Schools program, a movement aiming to support youth through educational services and mentorship. Mendes encouraged his fans to help the cause while giving the donors a chance to attend his upcoming concert tour.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-151)

In September 2018, Mendes took part in the annual [Global Citizen Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Citizen_Festival "Global Citizen Festival") held at [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-152) He performed, alongside other artists such as Janelle Monáe, John Legend, and Janet Jackson, and raised awareness regarding the importance of education and children's lack of access to education around the world, particularly young women. Ahead of the event, he took to social media to reach out to Canada's Prime Minister [Justin Trudeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Trudeau "Justin Trudeau"), thanking the Prime Minister for leading the initiative for Leave No Girl Behind, a movement whose goal is to empower girls through workshops and programs,[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-153) and expressing his willingness to talk more about the project. He also encouraged his fans to support the movement. In response, the Prime Minister thanked Mendes and stated "The more people we have fighting for girls' education, the better! Let's talk."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-154)

In October 2018, Mendes, together with producer Teddy Geiger, released a cover of "[Under Pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Pressure "Under Pressure")" by the British rock band [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)") and [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-155) The single was part of a series of covers of Queen's songs, released in celebration of Queen's biopic _[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-156) The proceeds from the single were donated to the [Mercury Phoenix Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Phoenix_Trust "Mercury Phoenix Trust"), an organization founded by Queen bandmembers after [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury")'s death, which helps fight against [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS").[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-157) Queen's manager, Jim Beach, expressed his gratitude to Mendes and Universal Music Group for helping the cause.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-158) On October 20, 2018, Mendes performed along with other artists such as Khalid, NF, Marshmello, Meghan Trainor, and Ella Mai at The [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") in Los Angeles for the "We Can Survive" event. The event was organized to raise funds for [Young Survival Coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Survival_Coalition "Young Survival Coalition"), in an effort to support young women who were diagnosed with [breast cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_cancer "Breast cancer").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-159)

In August 2019, Mendes announced the launch of the Shawn Mendes Foundation, aiming to "inspire and empower his fans and today's youth to bring about positive change in the world and advocate for issues they care most about."[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-160)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-161) On January 8, 2020, Mendes announced that both he and his Shawn Mendes Foundation would be donating an undisclosed sum of money to causes including the [Australian Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Red_Cross "Australian Red Cross"), the [New South Wales Rural Fire Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_Rural_Fire_Service "New South Wales Rural Fire Service"), and [South Australian Country Fire Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australian_Country_Fire_Service "South Australian Country Fire Service") to help ease the strain on those impacted by the devastating fires tearing through parts of the country.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-162) In March 2020 Mendes and The Shawn Mendes Foundation donated $175,000 to support COVID-19 relief to Toronto's SickKids Foundation, the largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care in Canada.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-163) Mendes and the Shawn Mendes Foundation announced Wonder Grants in December 2020 and have partnered with [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") to award the first set of Wonder Grants to young changemakers around the world. Wonder Grants aim to support and empower young creatives launching their projects across various fields, including music, film, education, science, environment, and technology.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-164) In January 2021, American chain of fast-casual restaurants [Chipotle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chipotle_Mexican_Grill "Chipotle Mexican Grill") announced its partnering with Mendes and his foundation to launch "Wonder Grants" supporting young innovators in sustainability, as well as a "Shawn Mendes Bowl" on the Chipotle app and Chipotle website for a limited time in the US and Canada. For every Shawn Mendes Bowl sold, Chipotle will donate $1 toward the foundation in support of changemakers and this marks the first time Chipotle has launched a philanthropic entrée on its menu.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-165) In June 2023, Mendes announced he collaborated with America luxury jewelry brand [David Yurman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yurman "David Yurman") and helped to design a woven hemp bracelet to benefit his foundation after previously announced as brand ambassador for the brand earlier this year. As part of the collaboration, 20% of the purchase price from the David Yurman bracelet will go to the foundation.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-166) Mendes has partnered with American subscription streaming service [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") as a tour sponsor for his [Wonder tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder:_The_World_Tour "Wonder: The World Tour") by visiting children's hospitals in the US. Mendes also planned to donate one dollar per ticket sold in North America towards his foundation's "Wonder Grants" program, which he would award to one "youth changemaker" in every city the tour visited.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-167)

In March 2020, Mendes participated in [iHeart Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeart_Media "IHeart Media")'s [Living Room Concert for America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeart_Living_Room_Concert_for_America "IHeart Living Room Concert for America"), a benefit to raise awareness and funds for the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-168) In March and April 2020, Mendes participated in Global Citizen Festival's Together at Home virtual concert to raise awareness and funds for the COVID-19 pandemic.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-169)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-170)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-171) Mendes has shown support for the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement. In May 2020 he, alongside [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello"), joined protests in Miami for racial justice after the [murder of George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd"), and has lent his [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") to raise the voice of Black activists.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-172)

On April 22, 2021, Mendes hosted a [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") video conference with the crew of [Expedition 65](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_65 "Expedition 65") on board the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station"). The televised event covered a Q&A with students and children about various topics related to [Earth Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_Day "Earth Day"), such as climate change, Earth observations, and general physics, as well as the astronauts' experience on the space station.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-173)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-175) In June 2021, Mendes, along with several other celebrities, signed an open letter to the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"), urging lawmakers to pass the [Equality Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equality_Act_(United_States) "Equality Act (United States)"). The artists, including Mendes, said of the Act that it would "protect ... the most marginalized communities".[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-176)

In May 2021, Mendes joined Cabello and [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") actors to help fight the [COVID-19 pandemic in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India "COVID-19 pandemic in India") during its peak of cases. Mendes donated $50,000 through the organization _Give India_.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-177)

## Personal life

Mendes resides in [downtown Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Toronto "Downtown Toronto").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-178) He began dating American singer [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello") in July 2019.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-179) Their relationship sparked controversy, as both were accused of attempting to start a relationship [for publicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publicity_stunt "Publicity stunt"),[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Capital_2019-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Bonner_2019-182) but Mendes insisted it was "definitely not a publicity stunt".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-Elle-183) The couple announced their split in November 2021.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-184) Mendes briefly dated [Sabrina Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter "Sabrina Carpenter") in early 2023.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-185) Since late 2025, Mendes has been in a relationship with [Bruna Marquezine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruna_Marquezine "Bruna Marquezine"), a Brazilian model and actress.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-186)

Regarding speculations about his [sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation"), in June 2016, Mendes stated: "First of all, I'm not gay. Second of all, it shouldn't make a difference if I was or if I wasn't. The focus should be on the music and not my sexuality."[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-188)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-189)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-190) In late October 2024, he commented that he was "still figuring out" his sexuality.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-191)

Mendes has been open about his struggles with [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder"), which he disclosed publicly in his song "[In My Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Blood_(Shawn_Mendes_song) "In My Blood (Shawn Mendes song)")". He said, "I spoke to a therapist a couple of times. [...] Therapy is what works for you. Therapy is listening to music and running on the treadmill, therapy is going to dinner with your friends—it's something that distracts you, that helps you heal and so it just depends on what you think therapy is. I made a conscious effort to be more connected to the people in my life. I found I was closing myself off from everybody, thinking that would help me battle it then realizing the only way I was going to battle it was completely opening up and letting people in."[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-192)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes#cite_note-193)

## Accolades and achievements

The **Grammy Award for Best Music Video** is an accolade presented at the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), a ceremony that was established in 1958 and originally called the Gramophone Awards,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-Grammy-1) to performers, directors, and producers of quality short form [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"). Honors in several categories are presented at the ceremony annually by the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences") of the United States to "honor artistic achievement, technical proficiency and overall excellence in the recording industry, without regard to album sales or chart position".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-Overview-2)

Originally called the **Grammy Award for Best Video, Short Form**, the award was first presented in 1984, as was a similar award for [Best Long Form Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Long_Form_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video"). From 1986 to 1997, the category name was changed to **Best Music Video, Short Form**. However, in 1988 and 1989, the award criteria were changed and the video awards were presented under the categories [Best Concept Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Concept_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Concept Music Video") and [Best Performance Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Performance_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Performance Music Video"). The awards were returned to the original format in 1990. The category was called **Best Short Form Music Video** until 2012, from 2013 it was shortened to **Best Music Video**.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-3) Award recipients include the performers, directors, and producers associated with the winning videos, except for its first two years when the Grammy went to the performing artist only. For unknown reasons, the award for the Best Music Video in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Grammy_Awards "1987 Grammy Awards") - _Brothers in Arms_ by [Dire Straits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dire_Straits "Dire Straits") - went to the band only, not to the director(s) or producer(s).

[Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") holds the record for the most wins as a performer in this category, with three. [Mark Romanek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Romanek "Mark Romanek") holds the record for the most wins as a director, with a total of three. Icelandic singer [Björk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bj%C3%B6rk "Björk") holds the record for the most nominations as a performer without a win, with four. [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") became the first artist to win the category with a sole directing credit for their own music video when she won in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards") for _[All Too Well: The Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_Too\_Well:\_The\_Short\_Film "All Too Well: The Short Film")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-4)

Honor presented for quality music videos

Not to be confused with [Grammy Award for Best Music Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Film "Grammy Award for Best Music Film").

The **Grammy Award for Best Music Video** is an accolade presented at the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), a ceremony that was established in 1958 and originally called the Gramophone Awards,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-Grammy-1) to performers, directors, and producers of quality short form [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"). Honors in several categories are presented at the ceremony annually by the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences") of the United States to "honor artistic achievement, technical proficiency and overall excellence in the recording industry, without regard to album sales or chart position".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-Overview-2)

Originally called the **Grammy Award for Best Video, Short Form**, the award was first presented in 1984, as was a similar award for [Best Long Form Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Long_Form_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video"). From 1986 to 1997, the category name was changed to **Best Music Video, Short Form**. However, in 1988 and 1989, the award criteria were changed and the video awards were presented under the categories [Best Concept Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Concept_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Concept Music Video") and [Best Performance Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Performance_Music_Video "Grammy Award for Best Performance Music Video"). The awards were returned to the original format in 1990. The category was called **Best Short Form Music Video** until 2012, from 2013 it was shortened to **Best Music Video**.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-3) Award recipients include the performers, directors, and producers associated with the winning videos, except for its first two years when the Grammy went to the performing artist only. For unknown reasons, the award for the Best Music Video in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Grammy_Awards "1987 Grammy Awards") - _Brothers in Arms_ by [Dire Straits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dire_Straits "Dire Straits") - went to the band only, not to the director(s) or producer(s).

[Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") holds the record for the most wins as a performer in this category, with three. [Mark Romanek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Romanek "Mark Romanek") holds the record for the most wins as a director, with a total of three. Icelandic singer [Björk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bj%C3%B6rk "Björk") holds the record for the most nominations as a performer without a win, with four. [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") became the first artist to win the category with a sole directing credit for their own music video when she won in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards") for _[All Too Well: The Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_Too\_Well:\_The\_Short\_Film "All Too Well: The Short Film")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Video#cite_note-4)

[2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards") winner [Childish Gambino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Glover "Donald Glover") for "[This is America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_America_(song) "This Is America (song)")".

**Taylor Alison Swift** (born December 13, 1989) is an American singer-songwriter. [An influential figure in popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_Taylor_Swift "Cultural impact of Taylor Swift"), Swift is known for her autobiographical songwriting and artistic reinventions. She is the [highest-grossing live music artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_live_music_artists "List of highest-grossing live music artists"), the [wealthiest female musician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_music_artists_by_net_worth "List of music artists by net worth"), and one of the [best-selling music artists of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-selling_music_artists_of_all_time "Best-selling music artists of all time").

Swift signed with [Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") in 2005 and debuted as a [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer with the albums _[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor\_Swift\_(album) "Taylor Swift (album)")_ (2006) and _[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Fearless (Taylor Swift album)")_ (2008). The singles "[Teardrops on My Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teardrops_on_My_Guitar "Teardrops on My Guitar")", "[Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Story_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Love Story (Taylor Swift song)")", and "[You Belong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Belong_with_Me "You Belong with Me")" found [crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") success on [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_radio "Country radio") and [pop radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_radio "Pop radio") formats. Her songs began incorporating stronger [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") elements with _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak\_Now "Speak Now")_ (2010) and [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") styles with _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Red (Taylor Swift album)")_ (2012). She subsequently recalibrated her artistic identity from country to [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") with the [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop") album _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989\_(album) "1989 (album)")_ (2014), while ensuing media scrutiny inspired the [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music")-imbued _[Reputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation\_(album) "Reputation (album)")_ (2017). Through the 2010s, Swift accumulated the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles "[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Never_Ever_Getting_Back_Together "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together")", "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")", "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")", and "[Look What You Made Me Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do "Look What You Made Me Do")".

Shifting to [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") in 2018, Swift released the [eclectic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_music "Eclecticism in music") pop album _[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover\_(album) "Lover (album)")_ (2019) and [re-recorded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recorded "Re-recorded") four of her first six albums due to [a dispute with Big Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute"). She explored [indie folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_folk "Indie folk") on the 2020 albums _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Folklore (Taylor Swift album)")_ and _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_, followed by mellower pop subgenres on _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_ (2022) and _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tortured\_Poets\_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_ (2024), as well as [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock") on _[The Life of a Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Life\_of\_a\_Showgirl "The Life of a Showgirl")_ (2025). The singles "[Cardigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardigan_(song) "Cardigan (song)")", "[Willow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_(song) "Willow (song)")", "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well_(Taylor's_Version) "All Too Well (Taylor's Version)")", "[Anti-Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Hero_(song) "Anti-Hero (song)")", "[Cruel Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruel_Summer_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Cruel Summer (Taylor Swift song)")", "[Is It Over Now?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Is_It_Over_Now%3F "Is It Over Now?")", "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_(song) "Fortnight (song)")", "[The Fate of Ophelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fate_of_Ophelia "The Fate of Ophelia")", "[Opalite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opalite_(song) "Opalite (song)")", and "[I Knew It, I Knew You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Knew_It,_I_Knew_You "I Knew It, I Knew You")" topped the Hot 100. Her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eras_Tour "Eras Tour") (2023–2024) and its associated film, _[Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor\_Swift:\_The\_Eras\_Tour "Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour")_ (2023), are the [highest-grossing concert tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours") and [concert film of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film#Highest-grossing_concert_films "Concert film").

Swift is the only artist to have been named the [IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFPI_Global_Recording_Artist_of_the_Year "IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year") six times. A record eight of her albums have each sold over a million copies first-week in the US. Publications such as _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ and [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)") have ranked Swift among the greatest artists of all time. She is the first individual from [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts") to be named [_Time_ Person of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Person_of_the_Year "Time Person of the Year") (2023) and the youngest female inductee into the [Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Songwriters Hall of Fame") (2026). [Her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Taylor_Swift "List of awards and nominations received by Taylor Swift") include 14 [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards")—including a record four [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") wins—and a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award"). Swift is the most-awarded artist of the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), the [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards"), and the [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"). A subject of [extensive media coverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_image_of_Taylor_Swift "Public image of Taylor Swift"), she has a global fanbase known as [Swifties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swifties "Swifties").

## Life and career

### Early life

Taylor Alison Swift was born on December 13, 1989, in [West Reading, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Reading,_Pennsylvania "West Reading, Pennsylvania").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-1) She is named after the singer-songwriter [James Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Taylor "James Taylor");[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone20173-2) her parents chose a unisex name, hoping it would help her succeed in business.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grigoriadis-2009-3) Her father, Scott Kingsley Swift, was a [stockbroker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockbroker "Stockbroker") for [Merrill Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrill_Lynch "Merrill Lynch"), and her mother, Andrea Gardner Swift ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Finlay), worked as a [mutual fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_fund "Mutual fund") marketing executive.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJepson20131-4) Swift's younger brother, [Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Swift "Austin Swift"), is an actor who manages her film projects.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-5) Taylor and Austin are of Scottish, English, and German descent, with distant Irish and Italian ancestry; they are paternal great-great-grandchildren of [Charles Carmine Antonio Baldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Carmine_Antonio_Baldi "Charles Carmine Antonio Baldi"), a prominent Philadelphia businessman.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-9) Their maternal grandmother, [Marjorie Finlay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjorie_Finlay "Marjorie Finlay") ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Moehlenkamp), was an opera singer whose singing in church became one of Swift's earliest memories of music.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer20104-10)

During childhood, Swift spent her [holiday seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiday_season "Holiday season") on a [Christmas tree farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_tree_farm "Christmas tree farm") in Pennsylvania,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-11) and summers at her family's vacation home in [Stone Harbor, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Harbor,_New_Jersey "Stone Harbor, New Jersey"), where she occasionally performed acoustic songs at a local coffee shop.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-12) Raised Christian,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-13) she attended preschool and kindergarten at a [Montessori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montessori "Montessori") school run by the [Bernardine Sisters of St. Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardine_Sisters_of_St._Francis "Bernardine Sisters of St. Francis") before transferring to the Wyndcroft School in [Pottstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottstown,_Pennsylvania "Pottstown, Pennsylvania").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-15) When her family moved to [Wyomissing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyomissing "Wyomissing"), she attended [Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyomissing_Area_Junior/Senior_High_School "Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High School").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-17) At age nine, she aspired to a career in [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater"), performing at local festivals and in Berks Youth Theatre Academy productions,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-19) and traveling regularly to New York City for vocal and acting lessons.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarlin201914-21) After watching a documentary about [Faith Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Hill "Faith Hill"), she changed her goal and became determined to pursue a [country Tennessee").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-22)

At the age of 11, Swift traveled to Nashville with her mother to visit record labels and submit [demo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_(music) "Demo (music)") tapes of [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton") and [Dixie Chicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixie_Chicks "Dixie Chicks") karaoke covers.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-23) She was rejected by all the labels, which led her to focus on songwriting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-24) She started learning the guitar at the age of 12 with the help of a computer repairman and local musician who assisted Swift in writing an original song.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-25) In 2003, she and her parents started working with the talent manager Dan Dymtrow. With his help, Swift modeled for [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"), had an original song included on a [Maybelline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybelline "Maybelline") compilation CD, and was given an [artist development deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_development_deal "Artist development deal") from [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records") at 13.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201010-27) To help Swift break into the country music scene, her father transferred to Merrill Lynch's Nashville office when she was 14 years old, and the family relocated to [Hendersonville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville,_Tennessee "Hendersonville, Tennessee").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Widdicombe-2011-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Jo_Sales-2013-29) Swift attended [Hendersonville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hendersonville_High_School_(Tennessee) "Hendersonville High School (Tennessee)") for two years before transferring to Aaron Academy, which offered homeschooling.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grigoriadis-2009-3)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-31)

### 2004–2008: Career beginnings and _Taylor Swift_

[![Image 9: Taylor Swift speaking into a mic, wearing a white sundress while holding her framed album](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_at_Yahoo_2007_(cropped).jpg)

Swift promoting her debut album in 2007

Swift signed with [Sony/ATV Tree Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony/ATV_Music_Publishing "Sony/ATV Music Publishing") in 2004; at 14, she became the youngest person in that publishing company's history.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-32) In Nashville, she worked with experienced [Music Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Row "Music Row") songwriters, including [Liz Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liz_Rose "Liz Rose").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-34) Rose and Swift would write songs every Tuesday afternoon after school.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-35) After one year on the development deal, she left RCA Records, which was planning to keep her in development until she turned 18.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-36) Swift made this decision because she wanted to release the songs immediately to ensure that they still resonated with her teenage experiences.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201012-37)

Swift organized a showcase concert at the [Bluebird Cafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluebird_Cafe "Bluebird Cafe") on November 3, 2004; among the attendees was [Scott Borchetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Borchetta "Scott Borchetta"), a music executive who was planning to establish an [independent record label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_record_label "Independent record label") called [Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-38) She signed a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract") with Big Machine two weeks after the concert, on the condition that her albums would be self-written;[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201021-40) her father purchased a three-percent stake in the company.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-41) The contract was finalized by July 2005, when Swift ended her working relationship with Dymtrow.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-42) She spent four months near the end of 2005 recording her debut album, [_Taylor Swift_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_(album) "Taylor Swift (album)"), with the producer [Nathan Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Chapman_(record_producer) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Morris-2006-43)

Swift's debut single, "[Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw_(song) "Tim McGraw (song)")", was released in June 2006. She and her mother spent mid-2006 sending promotional copies of the song to [country radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_radio "Country radio") stations across the US.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-44)_Taylor Swift_ was released on October 24, 2006.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201029-45) On the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart, the album peaked at number five and spent 157 weeks on the chart—the longest chart run by an album in the 2000s.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-46) With _Taylor Swift_, she became the first female country music artist to write or co-write every track on a [platinum-certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum-certified "Platinum-certified") debut album.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-47) Swift promoted the album with a six-month radio tour and by [opening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_act "Opening act") for other country artists, including [Rascal Flatts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rascal_Flatts "Rascal Flatts") in 2006,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Morris-2006-43)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-48) and [George Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Strait "George Strait"),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-49)[Brad Paisley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Paisley "Brad Paisley"),[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-50) and [Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw "Tim McGraw") and Faith Hill in 2007.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-51) She opened for Rascal Flatts again in 2008,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-52) when she dated the singer [Joe Jonas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Jonas "Joe Jonas").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-53)

_Taylor Swift_ was supported by four more singles in 2007 and 2008: "[Teardrops on My Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teardrops_on_My_Guitar "Teardrops on My Guitar")", "[Our Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Song "Our Song")", "[Picture to Burn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picture_to_Burn "Picture to Burn")", and "[Should've Said No](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Should've_Said_No "Should've Said No")". "Our Song" and "Should've Said No" reached number one on the [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") chart; with the former single, Swift became the youngest person to single-handedly write and sing a number-one country single.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-54) "Teardrops on My Guitar" was Swift's breakthrough single on mainstream radio and charts, reaching the top 10 of the [Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Songs "Pop Songs"), [Adult Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Songs "Adult Pop Songs"), and [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_(chart) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") charts.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-55)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-56) Her next releases were the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music")[extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP) _[The Taylor Swift Holiday Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Taylor\_Swift\_Holiday\_Collection "The Taylor Swift Holiday Collection")_ in October 2007,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-57) and the [Walmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart")-exclusive EP _[Beautiful Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful\_Eyes "Beautiful Eyes")_ in July 2008.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-58) Swift became the youngest person to be awarded with the [Nashville Songwriters Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Songwriters_Association_International "Nashville Songwriters Association International")'s Songwriter/Artist of the Year in 2007.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-59)

### 2008–2010: _Fearless_

[![Image 10: Taylor Swift wearing a dark strapless dress with her hair pinned up](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg/250px-TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TaylorSwiftApr09.jpg)

Swift at the 2009 premiere of _[Hannah Montana: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah\_Montana:\_The\_Movie "Hannah Montana: The Movie")_. She had a cameo appearance in the film and wrote two songs for [its soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Montana:_The_Movie_(soundtrack) "Hannah Montana: The Movie (soundtrack)").

Swift's second album, _[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Fearless (Taylor Swift album)")_, was released on November 11, 2008, in North America,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer201051-60) and in March 2009 in other markets.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-61)_Fearless_ spent eleven weeks at number one on the _Billboard_ 200, becoming her first chart topping album and the longest-running number-one female country album; it was the best-selling album of 2009 in the US.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-63) The album's lead single, "[Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Story_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Love Story (Taylor Swift song)")", became the first country song to top the Pop Songs chart, and its third single, "[You Belong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Belong_with_Me "You Belong with Me")", was the first country song to top _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s all-genre [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_(chart) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-64)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-65) both reached the top five of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart and peaked atop the Hot Country Songs chart.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-3-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) Three other singles—"[White Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Horse_(Taylor_Swift_song) "White Horse (Taylor Swift song)")", "[Fifteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteen_(song) "Fifteen (song)")", "[Fearless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Fearless (Taylor Swift song)")"—all reached the top 10 of Hot Country Songs.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) In 2009, Swift opened for [Keith Urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Urban "Keith Urban")'s tour and embarked on her first headlining concert tour, the [Fearless Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_Tour "Fearless Tour") (2009–2010).[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-68)

_Fearless_ became the most-awarded country album of all time.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-69) It won the three highest awards for a country album: Album of the Year by both the [Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association_Awards "Country Music Association Awards") and [Academy of Country Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "Academy of Country Music Awards") in 2009, and [Best Country Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Album "Best Country Album") by the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") in 2010.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-70) At the Grammy Awards, _Fearless_ also won [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), and "White Horse" won [Best Country Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Song "Best Country Song") and [Best Female Country Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Female_Country_Vocal_Performance "Best Female Country Vocal Performance").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-71) Also in 2009, Swift was named Artist of the Year by both the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2009 "American Music Awards of 2009") and _Billboard_,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-73) and Entertainer of the Year by the Country Music Association Awards, becoming the youngest person to receive the honor.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-74) "You Belong with Me" won [Best Female Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Female_Video "Best Female Video") at the [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"). Her acceptance speech was interrupted by the rapper [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"), [an incident that became the subject of controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_MTV_Video_Music_Awards#Kanye_West%E2%80%93Taylor_Swift_incident "2009 MTV Video Music Awards") and widespread media coverage.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTECullen201633-75)

### 2010–2014: _Speak Now_ and _Red_

[![Image 11: Taylor Swift singing into a mic while playing a guitar, dressed in a purple dress](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_2011crop.jpg)

Swift on the [Speak Now World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour "Speak Now World Tour") in 2011

Swift wrote her third album, _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak\_Now "Speak Now")_, entirely by herself.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Caramanica-2010-88) Released on October 25, 2010,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-89) it debuted atop the US _Billboard_ 200 with over one million first-week copies sold—the highest single-week tally for a female country artist.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-90) Five of its singles—"[Mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mine_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Mine (Taylor Swift song)")", "[Back to December](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_December "Back to December")", "[Mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_(song) "Mean (song)")", "[Sparks Fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparks_Fly_(song) "Sparks Fly (song)")", and "[Ours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ours_(song) "Ours (song)")"—charted in the top three of Hot Country Songs; "Sparks Fly" and "Ours" reached number one.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2-67) "Mine" peaked at number three and was the album's highest-charting single on the _Billboard_ Hot 100,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-91) and "Mean" became its best-selling track.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-92) Swift supported the album with the [Speak Now World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_World_Tour "Speak Now World Tour") (2011–2012) and its accompanying live album, _[Speak Now World Tour – Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak\_Now\_World\_Tour\_%E2%80%93\_Live "Speak Now World Tour – Live")_ (2011).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-93)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-94)

In 2011, Swift was honored as Woman of the Year by _Billboard_,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Roland-2011-95) Entertainer of the Year by both the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-96) and Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-97) She again won Entertainer of the Year at the Academy of Country Music Awards in 2012.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-98) At the [54th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "54th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2012, "Mean" won Best Country Song and [Best Country Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Solo_Performance "Best Country Solo Performance").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-99) After the release of _Speak Now_, Swift briefly dated the actor [Jake Gyllenhaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Gyllenhaal "Jake Gyllenhaal").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2014-77)

On October 22, 2012, Swift released her fourth album, _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Red (Taylor Swift album)")_, which she produced with Chapman and several new collaborators, including [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Shellback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellback_(record_producer) "Shellback (record producer)"), [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_(musician) "Dan Wilson (musician)"), [Jeff Bhasker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bhasker "Jeff Bhasker"), [Dann Huff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dann_Huff "Dann Huff"), and [Butch Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butch_Walker "Butch Walker").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Lewis-2012-100)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Mansfield-2012-101) It debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 with 1.21 million sales, becoming the fastest-selling country album in US history.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-102)_Red_ was Swift's first number-one album in the UK.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-103) During the promotion of _Red_, Swift was romantically involved with the political heir [Conor Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family"), and subsequently the singer [Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Billboard-2014-77)

### 2014–2018: _1989_ and _Reputation_

Swift relocated from Nashville to New York City in March 2014 and transformed her image from country to [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") with her fifth album, _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989\_(album) "1989 (album)")_.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-116)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-117) She produced _1989_ with Martin, Shellback, Chapman, and new collaborators [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), [Imogen Heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imogen_Heap "Imogen Heap"), [Ryan Tedder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tedder "Ryan Tedder"), and [Ali Payami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Payami "Ali Payami").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-118) Released on October 27, 2014, the album spent eleven weeks at number one and one year in the top 10 of the _Billboard_ 200.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-120) It has sold 14 million copies worldwide, becoming Swift's best-selling album.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Winter-2022-121) Three of _1989_'s singles—"[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")", and "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")"—reached number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100; the first two made Swift [the first woman to replace herself at the top spot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-122) Two other singles—"[Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Style_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Style (Taylor Swift song)")" and "[Wildest Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildest_Dreams "Wildest Dreams")"—peaked at numbers six and five, making _1989_ the first album by Swift to have five consecutive top 10 singles on the Hot 100.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-123)

"Dick Clark") Award for Excellence at the American Music Awards in 2014,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-125)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-126) and "Bad Blood" won [Video of the Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recording_Registry "National Recording Registry") in 2026.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-131)

During the promotion of _1989_, Swift publicly opposed free [music streaming services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_streaming_service "Music streaming service") and their compensation of artists. She published an [op-ed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Op-ed "Op-ed") in _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wall\_Street\_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ in July 2014 to stress the importance of albums as a creative medium for artists,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-132) and, in November, removed her discography from ad-supported, free streaming platforms such as [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-133) Big Machine kept her music only on paid, subscription-required platforms.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Christman-2014-134) In a June 2015 open letter, Swift criticized [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") for not offering royalties to artists during its free three-month trial period and threatened to withdraw her music from the platform,[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-135) prompting [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") to announce that it would pay artists during the free trial period.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-136) Big Machine returned Swift's catalog to Spotify and other free streaming platforms in June 2017.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-137)

Swift dated the DJ [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") from March 2015 to June 2016.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-138) They co-wrote "[This Is What You Came For](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_What_You_Came_For "This Is What You Came For")", an [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") single by Harris featuring [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna"); Swift was initially credited under the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-139) Swift also wrote "[Better Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Man_(Little_Big_Town_song) "Better Man (Little Big Town song)")", recorded by [Little Big Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Big_Town "Little Big Town") in 2016, which won the Country Music Association Award for Song of the Year.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Ryan-2017-140) She wrote and recorded "[I Don't Wanna Live Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Wanna_Live_Forever "I Don't Wanna Live Forever")" with [Zayn Malik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zayn_Malik "Zayn Malik") for [the soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty_Shades_Darker:_Original_Motion_Picture_Soundtrack "Fifty Shades Darker: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack") to the 2017 film _[Fifty Shades Darker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty\_Shades\_Darker\_(film) "Fifty Shades Darker (film)")_; it peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, the highest for a [_Fifty Shades_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty_Shades_(film_series) "Fifty Shades (film series)") single.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-141)

[![Image 14: Taylor Swift wearing a sparkling snake-patterned bodysuit while performing onstage](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Reputation_Tour1_(cropped).jpg)

Swift on her [Reputation Stadium Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour "Reputation Stadium Tour") in 2018

In April 2016, Kanye West released the single "[Famous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famous_(Kanye_West_song) "Famous (Kanye West song)")", in which he references Swift in the line, "I made that bitch famous." Swift criticized West and said she never consented to the lyric, but West claimed that he had received her approval, and his then-wife, [Kim Kardashian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Kardashian "Kim Kardashian"), released video clips of Swift and West discussing the song amicably over the phone. Although the clips were proven to be purposefully edited,[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-142) the controversy made Swift a subject of an online "[cancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture "Cancel culture")" movement, in which her critics denounced her as a fake and calculating "snake".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-143) In late 2016, after briefly dating the actor [Tom Hiddleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hiddleston "Tom Hiddleston"), Swift began a six-year relationship with the actor [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn") and went on hiatus.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-144)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilkinson2017444-145)

In August 2017, Swift [countersued and won a case against David Mueller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_sexual_assault_trial "Taylor Swift sexual assault trial"), a former [radio jockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_jockey "Radio jockey"), who sued her for damages from loss of employment. Four years earlier, she informed Mueller's employer that he had sexually assaulted her by groping her at an event.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-146) Public controversies influenced Swift's sixth album, _[Reputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation\_(album) "Reputation (album)")_, which explores themes of fame and finding love amidst the tumultuous affairs.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-147) Released on November 10, 2017,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-148)_Reputation_ debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200 with 1.21 million US sales and recorded first-week worldwide sales of two million copies.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-149)

_Reputation_'s lead single, "[Look What You Made Me Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_What_You_Made_Me_Do "Look What You Made Me Do")", topped the _Billboard_ Hot 100 with the highest sales and streaming week of 2017,[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-150) and was Swift's first UK number-one single.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-151) The singles "[...Ready for It?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Ready_for_It%3F "...Ready for It?")", "[End Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_Game_(song) "End Game (song)")", and "[Delicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicate_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Delicate (Taylor Swift song)")" were released to pop radio and all peaked in the top 20 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-152) In 2018, Swift featured on [Sugarland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarland "Sugarland")'s "[Babe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_(Sugarland_song) "Babe (Sugarland song)")" and embarked on the [Reputation Stadium Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_Stadium_Tour "Reputation Stadium Tour"), which grossed $345.7 million worldwide.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-153)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-154)

### 2018–2021: _Lover_, _Folklore_, and _Evermore_

In November 2018, Swift signed a record deal with [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), which promoted her albums under [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records")' imprint.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-155) The contract included a provision allowing Swift to maintain ownership of her [master recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_recording "Master recording"). In addition, if Universal sold any part of its stake in Spotify, it agreed to distribute a non-recoupable portion of the proceeds to its artists.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-157)

[![Image 15: A portrait of Swift](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png/250px-191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:191125_Taylor_Swift_at_the_2019_American_Music_Awards.png)

Swift at the [American Music Awards of 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2019 "American Music Awards of 2019"), where she was named Artist of the Decade

Swift's first album with Republic Records and seventh overall, _[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover\_(album) "Lover (album)")_, was released on August 23, 2019.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-158) She produced the album with Antonoff, [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), [Frank Dukes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Dukes "Frank Dukes"), and [Joel Little](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Little "Joel Little").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Catucci-2019-159)_Lover_ peaked atop the charts of such countries as Australia, Canada, Ireland, Mexico, Norway, Sweden, the UK, and the US,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-160) and was the global best-selling album by a solo artist of 2019.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-161) Three of its singles—"[Me!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me! "Me!")", "[You Need to Calm Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Need_to_Calm_Down "You Need to Calm Down")", and "[Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Lover (Taylor Swift song)")"—were released in 2019 and peaked in the top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100. "[The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man_(Taylor_Swift_song) "The Man (Taylor Swift song)")" was released in 2020 and charted highly, and "[Cruel Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruel_Summer_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Cruel Summer (Taylor Swift song)")" became a resurgent success in 2023, reaching number one.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-162) Swift promoted _Lover_ with the one-off [City of Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Lover "City of Lover") concert, [its accompanying television special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Lover#Video_and_music_releases "City of Lover"), and the live album _[Lover (Live from Paris)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover\_(Live\_from\_Paris) "Lover (Live from Paris)")_, which set the record for the largest vinyl sales week by a live album in the US.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-bb2025-164)

In 2019, Swift was named Artist of the Decade by the American Music Awards and Woman of the Decade by _Billboard_,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-165)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-166) and became the first female artist to win the MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year for a self-directed video, with "You Need to Calm Down".[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-167) During the promotion of _Lover_, Swift became embroiled in [a public dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute") with the talent manager [Scooter Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_Braun "Scooter Braun") after he purchased Big Machine Records, including the masters of her albums under the label.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grady-2019-168) Swift said that Big Machine would allow her to acquire the masters only if she exchanged one new album for each older one under a new contract, which she declined.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Grady-2019-168) In November 2020, Swift began [re-recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recording_(music) "Re-recording (music)") her back catalog to control the licensing of her songs for [commercial use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchronization_rights "Synchronization rights").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-169)

In February 2020, Swift signed a global publishing deal with [Universal Music Publishing Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Publishing_Group "Universal Music Publishing Group") after her 16-year contract with Sony/ATV expired.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-170) During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Swift collaborated with Antonoff and [Aaron Dessner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Dessner "Aaron Dessner") on two "sister albums" [surprise-released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") in 2020: _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Folklore (Taylor Swift album)")_ on July 24, and _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_ on December 11.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-171) Joe Alwyn co-wrote and co-produced several songs under the pseudonym William Bowery.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-172) Both albums incorporate atmospheric [indie folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_folk "Indie folk") and [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock") sounds with "Orchestration");[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Doyle-2021-173)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGrath202379FogartyArnold20215-174) radio—"[Cardigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardigan_(song) "Cardigan (song)")", "[Betty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Betty (Taylor Swift song)")", and "[Exile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exile_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Exile (Taylor Swift song)")" from _Folklore_, and "[Willow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_(song) "Willow (song)")", "[No Body, No Crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Body,_No_Crime "No Body, No Crime")", and "[Coney Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coney_Island_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Coney Island (Taylor Swift song)")" Swift won Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards in 2020[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-179) and Album of the Year for _Folklore_ at the [63rd Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards") in 2021, becoming the first woman to win the Grammy Award for Album of the Year three times.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-180) She played [Bombalurina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombalurina "Bombalurina") in the musical fantasy film _[Cats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cats\_(2019\_film) "Cats (2019 film)")_ (2019), for which she co-wrote and recorded the original song "[Beautiful Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful_Ghosts "Beautiful Ghosts")".[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-181) The documentary _[Miss Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss\_Americana "Miss Americana")_, which chronicled parts of Swift's life and career, premiered at the [2020 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Sundance_Film_Festival "2020 Sundance Film Festival") and received positive reviews.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-182)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-183)

### 2021–2023: Re-recordings and _Midnights_

[![Image 16: Taylor Swift singing into a mic, dressed in a two-piece leather outfit](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_2022_infobox.jpg)

Swift performing in 2022

Swift released two re-recorded albums in 2021: _[Fearless (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless\_(Taylor's\_Version) "Fearless (Taylor's Version)")_ on April 9, and _[Red (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor's\_Version) "Red (Taylor's Version)")_ on November 12. Both peaked atop the _Billboard_ 200; the former was the first re-recorded album to do so.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-184) The latter helped Swift become the female musician with the most weeks at number one on the [Top Country Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Country_Albums "Top Country Albums") chart, and its song "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well_(Taylor's_Version) "All Too Well (Taylor's Version)")" became the longest song to top the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-185)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-186)

Swift's tenth album, _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_, was released on October 21, 2022.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-The_Guardian-2022-187)_Midnights_ was Swift's fifth album to open atop the _Billboard_ 200 chart with US first-week sales of one million. Its tracks, led by the single "[Anti-Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Hero_(song) "Anti-Hero (song)")", made her the first artist to occupy the entire top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100 the same week.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-Dailey-2022-188) The album peaked atop the charts of at least 14 other countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Norway, and Sweden.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-189) Two other singles, "[Lavender Haze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavender_Haze "Lavender Haze")" and "[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Karma (Taylor Swift song)")", both peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-190)

Both debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200, and the former made Swift the female artist with the most number-one albums on the chart.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-191)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-192) The single "[Is It Over Now?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Is_It_Over_Now%3F "Is It Over Now?")" from _1989 (Taylor's Version)_ reached number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, making Swift the first woman to have three number-one songs from three different albums in a calendar year.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-193) Swift featured on [Big Red Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Red_Machine_(band) "Big Red Machine (band)")'s "[Renegade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renegade_(Big_Red_Machine_song) "Renegade (Big Red Machine song)")" Alcott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alcott "The Alcott")" (2023).[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-197) She wrote and recorded "[Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Carolina (Taylor Swift song)")" for [the soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_the_Crawdads_Sing_(soundtrack) "Where ### 2023–present: The Eras Tour, _The Tortured Poets Department_, and _The Life of a Showgirl_

In March 2023, Swift embarked on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), which she conceived as a tribute to her entire discography. The tour spanned five continents through December 2024.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift#cite_note-209) It exerted [a global cultural, economic, and political impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_Eras_Tour "Impact of the Eras Tour") and culminated in an unprecedented height of popularity for
