_**All Too Well: The Short Film**_ is a 2021 [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film")[romantic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_drama "Romantic drama")[short film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_film "Short film") written and directed by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift in her filmmaking debut. A [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_adaptation "Film adaptation") of her critically-acclaimed song "[All Too Well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well "All Too Well")" (2012), it is set against the backdrop of the uncut, [10-minute version of the song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well_(10_Minute_Version) "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)") released in 2021. It stars [Sadie Sink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadie_Sink "Sadie Sink") and [Dylan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_O'Brien "Dylan O'Brien") as a romantic couple whose up-and-down relationship ultimately falls apart, compounded by their [age gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_gap "Age gap"). Swift cited the works of [Barbara Stanwyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Stanwyck "Barbara Stanwyck"), [John Cassavetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cassavetes "John Cassavetes"), and [Noah Baumbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Baumbach "Noah Baumbach") as artistic influences upon the film.

Produced by Saul Germaine and [Taylor Swift Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_Productions "Taylor Swift Productions"), _All Too Well: The Short Film_ was released on November 12, 2021, in select theaters by [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") and on YouTube by [UMG's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group")[PolyGram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PolyGram "PolyGram") Entertainment and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"), in conjunction with Swift's second re-recorded album, _[Red (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor's\_Version) "Red (Taylor's Version)")_. After a premiere at the [AMC Theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_Theatres "AMC Theatres") in [Lincoln Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Square,_Manhattan "Lincoln Square, Manhattan"), New York City, it had a [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release") in major cities as well as special screenings at the 2022 [Tribeca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") and [Toronto film festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival"). It received critical acclaim, with particular praise directed towards Swift's direction as a debut filmmaker as well as the acting, script, drama, and production values.

The film garnered several awards and nominations from music and film organizations, including an [American Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award_for_Favorite_Music_Video "American Music Award for Favorite Music Video"), a [Hollywood Critics Association Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Critics_Association "Hollywood Critics Association"), an [Art Directors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Directors_Guild_Award "Art Directors Guild Award") and a Grammy Award for Best Music Video; at the [2022 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2022 MTV Video Music Awards"), it won [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") and [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Direction "Best Direction"), making Swift the first artist in [VMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards") history to win Best Direction for a self-directed work.

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

_All Too Well: The Short Film_ is a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_adaptation "Film adaptation") of the 10-minute version of the song "[All Too Well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well "All Too Well")" by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Pooley-2022-1) It also functions as a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for the song.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Setoodeh-2021-2) A literary quote from the Chilean poet [Pablo Neruda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Neruda "Pablo Neruda")—"Love is so short, forgetting is so long", from his poem "[Puedo Escribir Los Versos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_Love_Poems_and_a_Song_of_Despair "Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair")"—opens the film.[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-4) The story chronicles the relationship of two doomed lovers, Her and Him, compounded by an [age gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_gap "Age gap").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-5) "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)" plays throughout the film, except during a dialogued conflict between Her and Him.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Grein-2022-6) The song details a blooming romance between two people and its subsequent dissolution and resulting heartbreak.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Willman-2021-7) The nearly 15-minute film is divided into seven chapters—"An Upstate Escape", "The First Crack in the Glass", "Are You Real?", "The Breaking Point", "The Reeling", "The Remembering", and the [epilogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epilogue "Epilogue") "Thirteen Years Gone"—describing the relationship between Her and Him through various phases.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Doria-2021-8)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Plot")]

The story starts with the couple lying in bed together, Her ([Sadie Sink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadie_Sink "Sadie Sink")) mesmerized by Him ([Dylan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_O'Brien "Dylan O'Brien")).[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-11) They venture into [upstate New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstate_New_York "Upstate New York") in a car. Her leaves [her red scarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well#The_scarf "All Too Well") at a house belonging to Him's sister. Their relationship takes a turn at a dinner party, where Him ignores his girlfriend with a hand gesture, as he is busy catching up with his friends, making Her uncomfortable. They fight afterwards; Him is arrogant and dismissive, while a distraught Her is heartbroken but still wants to stay with Him. He apologizes and kisses Her to end the argument, and they dance in the refrigerator light. Him starts to distance himself from Her, eventually breaking up with her. A devastated Her weeps in bed, ignoring his phone calls. Her is seen typing on her [typewriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typewriter "Typewriter") and crumpling paper sheets. A montage shows Her alone at parties and sorrowful on her 21st birthday.[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-12) Him's life carries on as he walks alone down a [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") street, recalling some of the happier moments in his relationship with Her. The film then jumps 13 years into the future, where Her (Taylor Swift)[[note 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-13) has become an author and released her book _All Too Well_,[[note 5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-14) presumably detailing the heartache she went through with Him. She reads from the book to an audience in a packed bookstore. Outside the store, an older Him stands in the snow, watching Her through the window, wearing the same scarf she left behind 13 years ago.

## Conception and production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Conception and production")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Sadie_Sink_%2843914734441%29.jpg/250px-Sadie_Sink_%2843914734441%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sadie_Sink_(43914734441).jpg)

[![Image 7: Young man sitting in a chair](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Dylan_O%27Brien_in_2017_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Dylan_O%27Brien_in_2017_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dylan_O'Brien_in_2017_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)

[Sadie Sink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadie_Sink "Sadie Sink") (_left_) and [Dylan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_O'Brien "Dylan O'Brien") (_right_), both of whom were Swift's first choice to play the leads, instantly accepted the offer.

Swift stated via her social media that _All Too Well: The Short Film_ was shot on [35 mm film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35_mm_movie_film "35 mm movie film") by Japanese-Korean-British cinematographer [Rina Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rina_Yang "Rina Yang").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Bowenbank-2021-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-IndieWire-2021-16) Yang used an "[Arri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arri "Arri")[Arriflex 235](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arriflex_235 "Arriflex 235") for [handheld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand-held_camera "Hand-held camera") and [steadicam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steadicam "Steadicam"), and [Panavision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panavision "Panavision") MXL for dolly work"; lenses were Panavision Primo, with 11:1 Primo zoom. She shot exterior scenes on [Kodak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodak "Kodak")[Ektachrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ektachrome "Ektachrome")—the same kind she had used to shoot the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") television series _[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria\_(American\_TV\_series) "Euphoria (American TV series)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-17) Swift cited "[Barbara Stanwyck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Stanwyck "Barbara Stanwyck") films, particularly 1937's _[Stella Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stella\_Dallas\_(1937\_film) "Stella Dallas (1937 film)")",_ as artistic influences upon her film in addition to those of [John Cassavetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cassavetes "John Cassavetes") and [Noah Baumbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Baumbach "Noah Baumbach"), especially his [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") film _[Marriage Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage\_Story "Marriage Story")_ (2019), among other works.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-18)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-2022-19) She also mentioned the films _[The Way We Were](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Way\_We\_Were "The Way We Were")_ (1973), _[Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Story\_(1970\_film) "Love Story (1970 film)")_ (1970), and _[Kramer vs. Kramer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kramer\_vs.\_Kramer "Kramer vs. Kramer")_ (1979) as sources of inspiration.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-20)

Swift said she wanted tell a story about "girlhood [calcifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcification "Calcification") into this bruised adulthood" with the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-21) On _[Late Night with Seth Meyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Seth\_Meyers "Late Night with Seth Meyers"),_ she said she cast Sink and O'Brien because they were the only two people she imagined playing the roles, noting that she was a fan of O'Brien's works and that she would not have proceeded with making the film had Sink turned down the offer. Swift explained that she likes "working with friends or people who I think would be excited about working with me" and added that she was "just blown away by what [Sink and O'Brien] did—they went out and left it all on the field".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-22) Sink said she accepted Swift's offer without hesitation, as she was a fan of Swift, and was also interested in playing a "more rounded and mature" role while portraying her _[Stranger Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stranger\_Things "Stranger Things")_ character [Max Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Mayfield_(Stranger_Things) "Max Mayfield (Stranger Things)") during production of the series' [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stranger_Things_(season_4) "Stranger Things (season 4)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-23)[Shawn Levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Levy "Shawn Levy"), an executive producer for _Stranger Things_, makes a cameo appearance as the father of Sink's character in the short film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-25) Swift further revealed that Sink and O'Brien "were so electric and [improvising] a lot of what they were doing that we just couldn't take the camera off [them]".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Doria-2021-8) At the end of the film, Swift played an older version of Sink's character.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-26)

## Release and promotion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release and promotion")]

In June 2021, Swift announced that her re-recorded album, _[Red (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor's\_Version) "Red (Taylor's Version)")_, a re-recording of her fourth studio album _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_(Taylor\_Swift\_album) "Red (Taylor Swift album)")_ (2012), would be released on November 19, 2021; the release date was later moved up to November 12.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-27) It contains both the re-recorded version of the track "[All Too Well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well "All Too Well")" and its 10-minute uncut version as a bonus track "from the vault".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-28)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-29) On November 5, 2021, _[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Morning\_America "Good Morning America")_ revealed a teaser for the short film.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-31) The teaser featured a vintage car driving down on a quiet road surrounded by autumnal trees, as well as the names of the cast members.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Bowenbank-2021-15)_All Too Well: The Short Film_ is a dramatized account of the incidents and dynamics of the relationship described in the song.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Willman-2021-7) It is about "an effervescent, curious young woman who ends up completely out of her depth", stated Swift.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-32) She described it as an expression of her gratitude to her fans for their reception to the song "All Too Well" over the years.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Derschowitz-2021-33)

The film's world premiere took place on November 13 at the [AMC Theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_Theatres "AMC Theatres") in [Lincoln Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Square,_Manhattan "Lincoln Square, Manhattan"), New York City[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-34) with handpicked fans among those who attended.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Willman-2021-7) Each audience member received an autographed movie poster and a custom packet of tissues.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-35) Swift performed "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)" in the theatre after the screening.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Derschowitz-2021-33) The film was later released on the same day on YouTube, 13 hours after the album's release at midnight.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-36) It had a [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release") in major cities.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Russell-2021-37)

It was also screened in two film festivals. On June 11, 2022, _All Too Well: The Short Film_ had a special screening at the 2022 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") at the [Beacon Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beacon_Theatre_(New_York_City) "Beacon Theatre (New York City)") in New York City.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-38) The film was screened in its 35 mm form for the first time at the [2022 Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2022 Toronto International Film Festival") on September 9, 2022, at the [TIFF Bell Lightbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TIFF_Bell_Lightbox "TIFF Bell Lightbox") in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-2022-19)

A video of behind the scenes from the short film was released on December 8, 2022.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-39)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Critical response")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/Taylor_Swift_TIFF_2013.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_TIFF_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_TIFF_2013.jpg)

Swift's direction drew critical praise.

_All Too Well: The Short Film_ received acclaim from film critics,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-40)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Coates-2022-41)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Pooley-2022-1) with particular emphasis on Swift's vision as a filmmaker.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-42)_Variety_'s Ramin Setoodeh dubbed the short film "a music video on steroids meets a [Noah Baumbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Baumbach "Noah Baumbach") movie".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Setoodeh-2021-2) Brittany Spanos of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ called it a "dramatic and moving" film that "digs deep into heartache and [scarf lore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well#The_scarf "All Too Well")".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-43) Rhian Daly of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ said the film underscores "the emotional power of [Swift's] storytelling" with "devastating cinematography" and "electric performances" by Sink and O'Brien.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-44)[_Collider_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")'s Ryan Louis Mantilla reported that "Sink and O'Brien bring Swift's characters to life with vividly emotional performances telling an incredibly moving tale of love, power, [gaslighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaslighting "Gaslighting"), and heartache in the 15-minute film."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-45)

Karl Quinn, in his review for _[The Sydney Morning Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sydney\_Morning\_Herald "The Sydney Morning Herald")_, complimented the "gorgeously cliched _[Notebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Notebook "The Notebook")_-style" screenplay, Swift's direction, and the "finely tuned" performances of Sink and O'Brien.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Quinn-2021-46)[_Vogue_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_(magazine) "Vogue (magazine)")'s Sarah Spellings said many of the film's scenes felt like "in-jokes with the audience" and commended the midway dialogue featuring an argument between Sink and O'Brien's characters: "It felt less like a real fight and more like how you describe a fight to your friends later. In other words, it was a depiction of how a fight feels."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-47) In _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_, Patrick Ryan wrote that the film was "operatic in its emotions and scope" and felt the argument scene was "particularly gut-wrenching".[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-48)_[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Paul Grein also praised the argument, saying the writing in the scene is "so vivid that it's easy to see Swift winning an [Oscar for screenwriting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay") one day".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Grein-2022-6)

Laura Coates, publishing on _[RogerEbert.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com")_, commended Swift's direction, the "meticulous [lighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighting "Lighting") and eye for [production design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_design "Production design")", Yang's camerawork, and the "electric" chemistry between Sink and O'Brien. Coates highlighted the argument scene as well: "Though the instinct may be to emphasize the volatility of their relationship with quick, jarring cuts, the unflinching persistence of the [single take](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_take "Single take") means the viewer is left with nothing to do but squirm and despair as we watch their relationship fall apart before our eyes."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Coates-2022-41) In a less favorable review, Renaldo Matadeen of _[Comic Book Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic\_Book\_Resources "Comic Book Resources")_ described the film as a "powerful character portrait" with "great cinematography and clever pacing", but felt that Swift's appearance near the end as a grown Sink "takes away from the artistic, auteur feel" of the film, preventing it from being a "perfect [indie film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_film "Indie film")".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-49)

The film briefly had the highest rating on film review site [Letterboxd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letterboxd "Letterboxd") before _[Parasite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite\_(2019\_film) "Parasite (2019 film)")_ (2019) regained the status.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Russell-2021-37)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-IndieWire-2021-16)

### Commercial performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]

Following its release to YouTube, the film was the number-one trending video on the platform with over 14 million views.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-IndieWire-2021-16) It amassed 32 million views in its first three days.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Quinn-2021-46) The short film helped its source material, "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)", debut atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart, garnering Swift her eighth number-one song in the US, and the [longest song ever to top the chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Selected_additional_Hot_100_achievements "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones")—a feat recognized in _[Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness\_World\_Records "Guinness World Records")_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-50) As of September 2024, the film has over 101 million views on YouTube.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Davis-2022-51)

## Accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Accolades")]

_All Too Well: The Short Film_ has received awards recognition in a diverse set of fields. It was nominated in five categories at the [2022 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2022 MTV Video Music Awards"), including Swift's fifth nomination for [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year"),[[note 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-52)—a record tied with [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") for the most Video of the Year nominations;[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Grein-2022-6) Swift was also nominated for [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Direction "Best Direction") for a third consecutive year, following the music videos of "[The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man_(Taylor_Swift_song) "The Man (Taylor Swift song)")" in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2020 MTV Video Music Awards") and "[Willow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willow_(song) "Willow (song)")" in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2021 MTV Video Music Awards").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-53)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-54) The film won Video of the Year and [Best Longform Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Long_Form_Video "MTV Video Music Award for Best Long Form Video"), and Swift won Best Direction; she became the first artist to win Video of the Year three times, and the first artist to win Video of the Year for a self-directed video.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Montgomery-2022-55) She won four awards at the [2022 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2022 MTV Europe Music Awards"), including [Best Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Artist "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Artist") and [Best Pop Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Pop "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Pop") for the first time, and tied with [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") as the most awarded woman in [EMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "MTV Europe Music Awards") history (12 each).[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-56) Swift won six awards at the [2022 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2022 "American Music Awards of 2022"), including [Favorite Music Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "American Music Award for Video of the Year") and [Artist of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award_for_Artist_of_the_Year "American Music Award for Artist of the Year").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-AMAs_2022-57) In 2023, Swift became the first artist to win the Grammy Award for Best Music Video as sole director; it was her second win in the category after "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")" (2015).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-58)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

See also: [All Too Well §The scarf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well#The_scarf "All Too Well")

Publications have described the short film as one of the biggest newsmakers and [pop culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_culture "Pop culture") moments of 2021.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-68)[iHeartRadio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio "IHeartRadio") called it a "cultural sensation", and the short film also invited "[Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") buzz",[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-69)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-70)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-71)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-72)[Google searches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Search "Google Search") of Sink and O'Brien reached an all-time high upon its release.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-73) Various media outlets described the short film's absence from the shortlist for the 2023 [Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Live_Action_Short_Film "Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film") a snub.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-74)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-Davis-2022-51)

Canadian singer [Michael Bublé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bubl%C3%A9 "Michael Bublé"), in the music video for his 2022 single "I'll Never Not Love You", referenced and recreated iconic "love scenes" from various films with his wife, Luisana Lopilato; it included _All Too Well: The Short Film_, with Bublé as Him and Lopilato as Her.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-75)

The Department of English of the [Queen's University at Kingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_University_at_Kingston "Queen's University at Kingston"), a public [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario"), Canada, offers a [fall semester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_term "Academic term") course titled "Taylor Swift's Literary Legacy (Taylor's Version)", with a [syllabus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syllabus "Syllabus") requiring students to analyze many of Swift's works, such as _All Too Well: The Short Film,_ to understand their literary references and [sociopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociopolitical "Sociopolitical") relevance in contemporary culture.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-76)

Following the success of the short film, Swift was inspired to venture further into filmmaking.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-77)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-78) In December 2022, [Searchlight Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Searchlight_Pictures "Searchlight Pictures") announced that Swift has written an original script and will direct her debut [feature film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_film "Feature film"); details about the cast, plot, and title were withheld "until a later date".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-79) She took part in _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_'s Directors on Directors series opposite British-Irish filmmaker [Martin McDonagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_McDonagh "Martin McDonagh") to elucidate her filmmaking approach.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-80)

According to [Kodak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodak "Kodak"), the short film, which was photographed in 35mm [Ektachrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ektachrome "Ektachrome") by Yang, contributed to generating an "enormous interest" in the format.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well:_The_Short_Film#cite_note-81)

The **65th Annual Grammy Awards** ceremony was held at the [Crypto.com Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crypto.com_Arena "Crypto.com Arena") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on February 5, 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-2) It recognized the best recordings, compositions, and artists of the eligibility year – October 1, 2021 to September 30, 2022 – as determined by the members of [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences"). The nominations were announced on November 15, 2022.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-3) South African comedian [Trevor Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Noah "Trevor Noah"), who hosted the [63rd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards") and [64th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards") ceremonies, returned again.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-5)

[Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") received the most nominations (nine) and tied [Maverick City Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick_City_Music "Maverick City Music") for wins (four), followed by [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") with eight nominations and three wins, and [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele") and [Brandi Carlile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandi_Carlile "Brandi Carlile") with seven nominations each.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-6) With a career total of 88 nominations, Beyoncé tied with her husband [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") as the [most nominated artists in Grammy history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_records "Grammy Award records").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-7)[Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny")'s _[Un Verano Sin Ti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un\_Verano\_Sin\_Ti "Un Verano Sin Ti")_ (2022) became the first Spanish-language album to be nominated for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-8)

With her win in the [Best Dance/Electronic Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance/Electronic_Album "Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Album") category, Beyoncé passed Hungarian-British conductor [Georg Solti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Solti "Georg Solti") for the record of most Grammy awards in the ceremony's history, with 32.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-9)[Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles") won [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for _[Harry's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry's\_House "Harry's House")_, becoming the first male [British solo artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_British_Grammy_winners_and_nominees "List of British Grammy winners and nominees") to win since [George Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Michael "George Michael") in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "31st Annual Grammy Awards"). [Lizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizzo "Lizzo") won [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") for "[About Damn Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About_Damn_Time "About Damn Time")", becoming the first black woman to win the award since [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") in [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "36th Annual Grammy Awards"). [Bonnie Raitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Raitt "Bonnie Raitt") won [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") for "[Just Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Like_That_(Bonnie_Raitt_song) "Just Like That (Bonnie Raitt song)")", becoming the first female solo songwriter to win since [Amy Winehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Winehouse "Amy Winehouse") in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "50th Annual Grammy Awards"). [Samara Joy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samara_Joy "Samara Joy") won [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), becoming the first jazz artist to win the award since [Esperanza Spalding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esperanza_Spalding "Esperanza Spalding") in [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "53rd Annual Grammy Awards"). [Sam Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Smith "Sam Smith") and [Kim Petras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Petras "Kim Petras") won [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance") for "[Unholy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unholy_(Sam_Smith_and_Kim_Petras_song) "Unholy (Sam Smith and Kim Petras song)")", making Petras the first transgender artist to win the award.

With her win in the [Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Audio_Book,_Narration_&_Storytelling_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording") category, [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis") became the 18th person to win the [EGOT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EGOT "EGOT") in her entertainment career.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-10)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

For the 2023 ceremony, the academy announced several changes for different categories and eligibility rules:[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-changes-11)

### Category changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Category changes")]

*   Five categories– [Best Alternative Music Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Alternative_Music_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Performance"), [Best Americana Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Americana_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Americana Performance"), [Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Score_Soundtrack_for_Video_Games_and_Other_Interactive_Media "Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media"), [Best Spoken Word Poetry Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Spoken_Word_Poetry_Album "Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Poetry Album"), and [Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Songwriter_of_the_Year,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical")– were added.
*   A Special Merit Award, Best Song for Social Change, was added. The award will be determined by a Blue Ribbon Committee and is destined to reward songs that "contain lyrical content that addresses a timely social issue and promotes understanding, peacebuilding and empathy".
*   For the categories of [Best Opera Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Opera_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Opera Recording") and [Best Classical Compendium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Classical_Compendium "Grammy Award for Best Classical Compendium"), composers and [librettists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Librettist "Librettist") became eligible for the award.
*   [Best New Age Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Age,_Ambient_Or_Chant_Album "Grammy Award for Best New Age, Ambient Or Chant Album") was renamed Best New Age, Ambient or Chant Album.
*   For [Best Musical Theater Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Musical_Theater_Album "Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album"), composers and lyricists of more than 50% of the score of a new recording became eligible for the award.
*   [Best Spoken Word Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Audio_Book,_Narration_&_Storytelling_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording") was renamed Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording. Spoken word poetry is no longer eligible for this award and is now recognized with the [Best Spoken Word Poetry Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Spoken_Word_Poetry_Album "Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Poetry Album") category.

### Album eligibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Album eligibility")]

*   In order to be eligible for consideration, albums must contain greater than 75% playing time of newly recorded music; the previous eligibility rule was 50%. This rule does not apply to the categories of [Best Compilation Soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Compilation_Soundtrack_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media"), [Best Historical Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Historical_Album "Grammy Award for Best Historical Album"), [Best Immersive Audio Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Immersive_Audio_Album "Grammy Award for Best Immersive Audio Album"), [Best Recording Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Recording_Package "Grammy Award for Best Recording Package"), [Best Special Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Boxed_or_Special_Limited_Edition_Package "Grammy Award for Best Boxed or Special Limited Edition Package"), and [Best Album Notes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Album_Notes "Grammy Award for Best Album Notes").

### Craft committees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Craft committees")]

*   For three categories of the classical music field ([Producer of the Year, Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Producer_of_the_Year,_Classical "Grammy Award for Producer of the Year, Classical"), [Best Engineered Album, Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Engineered_Album,_Classical "Grammy Award for Best Engineered Album, Classical") and [Best Contemporary Classical Composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Contemporary_Classical_Composition "Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Classical Composition")) the nominations will be determined by specialized craft committees.

The **65th Annual Grammy Awards** ceremony was held at the [Crypto.com Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crypto.com_Arena "Crypto.com Arena") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on February 5, 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-2) It recognized the best recordings, compositions, and artists of the eligibility year – October 1, 2021 to September 30, 2022 – as determined by the members of [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences"). The nominations were announced on November 15, 2022.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-3) South African comedian [Trevor Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Noah "Trevor Noah"), who hosted the [63rd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards") and [64th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards") ceremonies, returned again.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-5)

[Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") received the most nominations (nine) and tied [Maverick City Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick_City_Music "Maverick City Music") for wins (four), followed by [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") with eight nominations and three wins, and [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele") and [Brandi Carlile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandi_Carlile "Brandi Carlile") with seven nominations each.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-6) With a career total of 88 nominations, Beyoncé tied with her husband [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") as the [most nominated artists in Grammy history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_records "Grammy Award records").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-7)[Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny")'s _[Un Verano Sin Ti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un\_Verano\_Sin\_Ti "Un Verano Sin Ti")_ (2022) became the first Spanish-language album to be nominated for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-8)

With her win in the [Best Dance/Electronic Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance/Electronic_Album "Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Album") category, Beyoncé passed Hungarian-British conductor [Georg Solti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Solti "Georg Solti") for the record of most Grammy awards in the ceremony's history, with 32.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-9)[Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles") won [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for _[Harry's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry's\_House "Harry's House")_, becoming the first male [British solo artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_British_Grammy_winners_and_nominees "List of British Grammy winners and nominees") to win since [George Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Michael "George Michael") in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "31st Annual Grammy Awards"). [Lizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizzo "Lizzo") won [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") for "[About Damn Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About_Damn_Time "About Damn Time")", becoming the first black woman to win the award since [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") in [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "36th Annual Grammy Awards"). [Bonnie Raitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Raitt "Bonnie Raitt") won [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") for "[Just Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Like_That_(Bonnie_Raitt_song) "Just Like That (Bonnie Raitt song)")", becoming the first female solo songwriter to win since [Amy Winehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Winehouse "Amy Winehouse") in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "50th Annual Grammy Awards"). [Samara Joy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samara_Joy "Samara Joy") won [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), becoming the first jazz artist to win the award since [Esperanza Spalding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esperanza_Spalding "Esperanza Spalding") in [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "53rd Annual Grammy Awards"). [Sam Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Smith "Sam Smith") and [Kim Petras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Petras "Kim Petras") won [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance") for "[Unholy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unholy_(Sam_Smith_and_Kim_Petras_song) "Unholy (Sam Smith and Kim Petras song)")", making Petras the first transgender artist to win the award.

With her win in the [Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Audio_Book,_Narration_&_Storytelling_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording") category, [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis") became the 18th person to win the [EGOT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EGOT "EGOT") in her entertainment career.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-10)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

For the 2023 ceremony, the academy announced several changes for different categories and eligibility rules:[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammys#cite_note-changes-11)

### Category changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Category changes")]

*   Five categories– [Best Alternative Music Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Alternative_Music_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Performance"), [Best Americana Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Americana_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Americana Performance"), [Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Score_Soundtrack_for_Video_Games_and_Other_Interactive_Media "Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media"), [Best Spoken Word Poetry Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Spoken_Word_Poetry_Album "Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Poetry Album"), and [Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Songwriter_of_the_Year,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical")– were added.
*   A Special Merit Award, Best Song for Social Change, was added. The award will be determined by a Blue Ribbon Committee and is destined to reward songs that "contain lyrical content that addresses a timely social issue and promotes understanding, peacebuilding and empathy".
*   For the categories of [Best Opera Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Opera_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Opera Recording") and [Best Classical Compendium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Classical_Compendium "Grammy Award for Best Classical Compendium"), composers and [librettists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Librettist "Librettist") became eligible for the award.
*   [Best New Age Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Age,_Ambient_Or_Chant_Album "Grammy Award for Best New Age, Ambient Or Chant Album") was renamed Best New Age, Ambient or Chant Album.
*   For [Best Musical Theater Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Musical_Theater_Album "Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album"), composers and lyricists of more than 50% of the score of a new recording became eligible for the award.
*   [Best Spoken Word Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Audio_Book,_Narration_&_Storytelling_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording") was renamed Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording. Spoken word poetry is no longer eligible for this award and is now recognized with the [Best Spoken Word Poetry Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Spoken_Word_Poetry_Album "Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Poetry Album") category.

### Album eligibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Album eligibility")]

*   In order to be eligible for consideration, albums must contain greater than 75% playing time of newly recorded music; the previous eligibility rule was 50%. This rule does not apply to the categories of [Best Compilation Soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Compilation_Soundtrack_for_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media"), [Best Historical Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Historical_Album "Grammy Award for Best Historical Album"), [Best Immersive Audio Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Immersive_Audio_Album "Grammy Award for Best Immersive Audio Album"), [Best Recording Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Recording_Package "Grammy Award for Best Recording Package"), [Best Special Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Boxed_or_Special_Limited_Edition_Package "Grammy Award for Best Boxed or Special Limited Edition Package"), and [Best Album Notes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Album_Notes "Grammy Award for Best Album Notes").

### Craft committees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Craft committees")]

*   For three categories of the classical music field ([Producer of the Year, Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Producer_of_the_Year,_Classical "Grammy Award for Producer of the Year, Classical"), [Best Engineered Album, Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Engineered_Album,_Classical "Grammy Award for Best Engineered Album, Classical") and [Best Contemporary Classical Composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Contemporary_Classical_Composition "Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Classical Composition")) the nominations will be determined by specialized craft committees.

The **UK Music Video Awards** is an annual celebration of [creativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity "Creativity"), technical excellence and [innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innovation "Innovation") in [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") and moving image for music. The awards began in 2008. There is a wide range of opportunities for [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") individuals and companies to enter their work: from genre-led video categories, to prizes for individuals in the technical and craft areas of the business, to recognition for innovative approaches to music videos, [ads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising "Advertising") and other visuals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards#cite_note-1) There are also awards for international videos and outstanding individuals, voted for by the MVA jury members.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards#cite_note-2) The Awards take place in the autumn, with the entry process opening in early August. The UK MVA's are originally the key members of the team behind BUG, the BFI Southbank's music video strand, and have 20 years’ experience running events in the UK music video business.

The **UK Music Video Awards** is an annual celebration of [creativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity "Creativity"), technical excellence and [innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innovation "Innovation") in [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") and moving image for music. The awards began in 2008. There is a wide range of opportunities for [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") individuals and companies to enter their work: from genre-led video categories, to prizes for individuals in the technical and craft areas of the business, to recognition for innovative approaches to music videos, [ads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising "Advertising") and other visuals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards#cite_note-1) There are also awards for international videos and outstanding individuals, voted for by the MVA jury members.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards#cite_note-2) The Awards take place in the autumn, with the entry process opening in early August. The UK MVA's are originally the key members of the team behind BUG, the BFI Southbank's music video strand, and have 20 years’ experience running events in the UK music video business.
